items.title: Review the GitHub Actions setup (build-N-test, build-Dev-Docker-Containers)
items.body:
Code review of `.github/workflows/` - build-N-test.yml and its matrix, build-Dev-Docker-Containers.yml and its matrix, and the
codeql / doxygen jobs: what is obsolete, what is missing, what is fragile.

One input, measured from the `df -h` output in every job of the last v3-Release run (33628502689) and today's v3-Dev run
(39356906082) - the lowest free space any job reached:

| Runner | Disk | Free at start | Lowest free | Most a build used |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Linux (in the container) | 145G | 75-81 GiB | 65 GiB (ubuntu-26.04-clang++-22-debug, g++-16) | 11 GiB |
| Windows (D:, workspace + docker) | 150G | 146 GiB | 89 GiB (vs2k22-msys-x86_64-All3rdParty-Debug) | 57 GiB |
| macOS-15 | 320Gi (shared APFS) | 41-43 GiB | 30 GiB (XCode-16.4-Debug) | 13 GiB |
| macOS-26 | 320Gi | 95 GiB | 86 GiB | 9 GiB |

So the space-saving steps and comments written when the Linux runners were short of disk ("Due to insufficient disk space
error on ubuntu-latest", the "Save space" steps, `extra_apt_add_packages` / `extra_apt_remove_packages`, the
smaller-container configs) are candidates to drop. macOS-15 has the least headroom. (`df` runs only between steps, so a
peak within one, such as the third-party build on Linux, is not seen.)

items.title: Linux test jobs spend minutes on broad disk cleanup

labels.name: type::bug
labels.description: describes erroneous operation, use severity::* to classify the type

labels.name: type::testing
labels.description: issues about tests or the test infrastructure

items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I added a descriptive title
- [x] I searched open reports and couldn't find a duplicate

### What happened?

The Linux test workflow removes a broad collection of system packages before running tests. Across the eight Linux test jobs in [this attempt](https://github.com/conda/conda-build/actions/runs/36753467582/attempts/1), cleanup took **1,082 seconds of combined runner time**. Individual jobs ranged from 32 to 386 seconds.

In [the slowest cleanup job](https://github.com/conda/conda-build/actions/runs/36753467582/job/110018260607), 320 of the 386 seconds were spent removing system packages. The jobs overlap, so 1,082 seconds is not elapsed workflow time.

**An implementation already exists in #5963, `ci: reduce test workflow overhead`.** This issue tracks that PR and the current measurements. Continue the existing work rather than introducing a second cleanup implementation.

Expected result: each Linux job does only the cleanup needed to complete its tests and save its cache reliably.

Done when:

- #5963 has been checked against the current workflow and its cleanup changes are in place.
- The largest Linux test workloads and the cache-save step complete without running out of space.
- Before/after cleanup duration and total job duration are recorded on comparable runners. Preserve swap, as established in #6140.

### Conda Info

This is runner setup before the test environment is installed. The relevant evidence is the Free Disk Space step in [the linked Linux job](https://github.com/conda/conda-build/actions/runs/36753467582/job/110018260607).

### Conda Config

The audited workflow uses [`.github/condarc`](https://github.com/conda/conda-build/blob/adea698b6435723f502eb21d1e624236e32e7c31/.github/condarc). Test-specific channel and cache settings are described above and in the linked source.

### Conda list

See the Conda List steps in [the referenced CI run or job](https://github.com/conda/conda-build/actions/runs/36753467582/job/110018260607) for the installed packages. Use the same dependency versions for before/after measurements.

### Additional Context

Part of #6180 and the Slow Test Review Initiative #6030.

[Current cleanup configuration](https://github.com/conda/conda-build/blob/adea698b6435723f502eb21d1e624236e32e7c31/.github/workflows/tests.yml#L124).

#5963 also adjusts where coverage options are configured. This ticket tracks its cleanup work. Its existing diff trims the removal list, but the effect on current runner images still needs measuring.

items.title: Open MPI shared-memory files persist after Khiops exits with KHIOPS_PROC_NUMBER=1
items.body:
### Description

On Linux, running Khiops with `KHIOPS_PROC_NUMBER=1` leaves Open MPI shared-memory files in `/dev/shm` after the process exits. The files have names such as `sm_segment.aa178b29b743.0.67e60000.0`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Check the contents of `/dev/shm`.
2. Run `KHIOPS_PROC_NUMBER=1 khiops -v`.
3. Check `/dev/shm` again.

A new `sm_segment.*` file remains after Khiops exits. The same behavior occurs when running scenarios.

### Impact

We use `khiops-python` to score small prediction models in a Kubernetes pod, with one processor per model. Each of four models invokes Khiops four times per minute. The leftover files are approximately 72 KiB each; they accumulate, and the pod is eventually killed for exceeding its memory limit.

### Workaround

Setting `OMPI_MCA_btl="self,tcp"` prevents the files from being left behind.

### Environment

- Khiops 11.0.1, reproduced with both the `pip` and native packages
- Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie)

<details>
<summary>Khiops environment output</summary>

```text
Khiops 11.0.1

Environment variables:
        KHIOPS_DRIVERS_PATH     /app/.venv/lib
Internal environment variables:
        None
Temporary file directory:       /tmp
System resources:
        Host number 1

        Available disk space on system 84.8 GB
        hostname        MPI ranks       logical memory  disk    cores
```

items.title: Release workflow fails on every main push: automata-oci-image build hits runner disk exhaustion
items.body:
### Expected behavior

The `Release` workflow on `main` builds and publishes the `automata-oci-image` containerdisk so fleet automata VMs receive their declared image updates (per the containerdisk rebuild path).

### Observed behavior

Every `Release` run on `main` since 2026-10-27 15:43Z fails in job `nix / Packages (x86_64-linux, ubuntu-latest, automata-oci-image)` with runner disk exhaustion while building the docker image tarball. Four consecutive failures: [40528346342](https://github.com/shikanime-labs/machines/actions/runs/40528346342), [40528540743](https://github.com/shikanime-labs/machines/actions/runs/40528540743), [40534394980](https://github.com/shikanime-labs/machines/actions/runs/40534394980), [40542125729](https://github.com/shikanime-labs/machines/actions/runs/40542125729). The automata image has not shipped since the last green release — the fleet image pipeline is down.

### Environment

```
- Repo: shikanime-labs/machines, workflow Release, push on main
- Job: nix / Packages (x86_64-linux, ubuntu-latest, automata-oci-image)
- Runner: ubuntu-latest hosted runner
```

### Evidence

```
error (ignored): write of 226 bytes: No space left on device
error: Cannot build '/nix/store/j4kb2pfq0824f5xf9smy9rapwgfhc550-docker-image-automata.tar.gz.drv'.
       Reason: builder failed with exit code 28.
note: build failure may have been caused by lack of free disk space
```

The failure lands at the `Adding layer...` / `Adding meta...` stage of the docker-image tarball assembly, i.e. the image grew past what the runner free space allows at that step (or the job does not reclaim space before the tar step).

### References

- None found in this repo for runner disk pressure on the release path.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The `Release` workflow is green on a `main` push — decidable with `gh run list -R shikanime-labs/machines -w Release --limit 1` showing `success`
- [ ] The root cause is recorded on this issue (image size growth vs runner capacity vs missing cleanup step) — decidable by a comment citing the failing step's disk usage (`df` output or the tar size vs runner free space)
- [ ] The fix prevents recurrence — decidable by two consecutive green `Release` runs after the change lands

items.title: Writable layer (persistence) for live ISOs
items.body:
Ventoy (USB) has persistence for live Linux; people ask for it on network boot too (settings and installed packages kept between boots).

**To decide / ideas**
- A per-PC or per-ISO writable image on the server (an overlay file) attached next to the ISO's network disk: casper `persistent` + a labelled ext4 volume over NBD, Debian live `persistence` the same way.
- Needs a read-write NBD/iSCSI export (today both are read-only), with locking so two PCs never share one file.
- Disk space management and a "reset" button.
- Which distributions: Ubuntu/Mint (casper), Debian live, Fedora, Arch (archiso `cow_device`). Probably a per-family feature.

Found in the competitor comparison of 2026-10-22 (iVentoy official news and edition pages, netboot.xyz and FOG documentation). Nothing is decided: this issue is for deciding whether and how to do it.

items.title: Kali Linux Cyber security lab -- troubleshooting
items.body:
This document covers common challenges encountered when setting up a Kali Linux cybersecurity lab using Oracle VirtualBox on a Windows host. It provides possible causes, troubleshooting steps, and lessons learned to help beginners build and maintain their own lab environments.

Lab environment

- Host OS: Windows
- Virtualization platform: Oracle VirtualBox
- Guest OS: Kali Linux
- Purpose: Cybersecurity learning, networking practice, and authorized security testing

«Note: These are common setup challenges and troubleshooting procedures. Only mark an issue as personally encountered if it occurred in your own lab.»

---

1. Virtual Machine Resource Allocation

Problem: Kali Linux may run slowly or become unresponsive inside VirtualBox.

Possible causes:

- Insufficient RAM allocated to the virtual machine.
- Too many virtual CPUs assigned.
- Limited disk space on the host.
- Too many applications running on Windows.

Solution:

- Allocate resources based on the host computer's available capacity.
- Leave enough RAM and CPU resources for Windows.
- Check available storage before expanding the virtual disk.
- Close unnecessary applications when running the VM.

Lesson learned: Proper resource allocation improves performance and stability without overloading the host.

---

2. Kali Linux Installation and Disk Partitioning

Problem: Beginners may be unsure which installation and partitioning options to select.

Possible causes:

- Unfamiliarity with guided partitioning.
- Confusion about encrypted LVM.
- Uncertainty about disk selection.

Solution:

- Confirm that the installer is targeting the intended VirtualBox virtual disk.
- Understand the difference between guided partitioning, manual partitioning, and encrypted LVM.
- Consider encrypted LVM when protecting stored data is a priority, while remembering that it adds password and recovery considerations.
- Back up important files before changing disk configurations.

Lesson learned: Virtual disks and physical disks are different, but selecting the wrong target can still cause data loss. Always verify the target before confirming destructive changes.

---

3. VirtualBox Network Adapter Configuration

Problem: Kali Linux cannot access the internet or communicate with other virtual machines.

Possible causes:

- Incorrect network adapter mode.
- Disabled virtual network adapter.
- Incorrect IP address or routing configuration.
- Network restrictions on the host.

Solution:

- Use NAT when the VM mainly needs outbound internet access.
- Use Host-only or Internal Network for isolated lab communication, depending on the topology.
- Use Bridged networking only when the VM needs to participate directly on the physical network and the risks are understood.
- Confirm the adapter is enabled and attached to the intended virtual network.

Useful commands:

ip addr
ip route

Lesson learned: Network adapter modes serve different purposes. The right choice depends on whether the lab needs internet access, host communication, or isolated VM-to-VM communication.

---

4. Promiscuous Mode Configuration

Problem: The promiscuous mode option may be unavailable, restricted, or fail to provide the expected packet visibility.

Possible causes:

- The selected adapter mode or VirtualBox configuration restricts the available options.
- The lab topology does not send the relevant traffic to the VM.
- The guest interface or packet-capture configuration is incorrect.

Solution:

- Review the selected adapter mode and VirtualBox settings.
- Use the least permissive setting that meets the exercise's requirements.
- For packet analysis, create a controlled lab topology and verify which traffic reaches the capture interface.
- Avoid assuming promiscuous mode automatically allows a VM to see all network traffic.

Lesson learned: Packet visibility depends on network topology and configuration, not just a single setting.

---

5. DNS and Name Server Configuration

Problem: Kali Linux can appear connected to a network but cannot resolve domain names.

Possible causes:

- Incorrect DNS server configuration.
- Missing or invalid network settings.
- Connectivity problems between the VM and its configured DNS resolver.

Solution:

Check the current network configuration:

cat /etc/resolv.conf
ip route

Test name resolution:

getent hosts kali.org

Compare the result with a connectivity test to a known reachable IP address:

ping -c 4 1.1.1.1

A failed ping alone does not prove that connectivity is unavailable, because some destinations block ICMP traffic.

Check the VirtualBox adapter and the guest's network configuration before changing DNS settings.

Lesson learned: DNS resolution and general network connectivity are separate issues and should be tested independently.

---

6. Clipboard Integration Between Windows and Kali Linux

Problem: Copy-and-paste does not work between the Windows host and Kali Linux guest.

Possible causes:

- Shared Clipboard is disabled.
- Guest integration components are missing or not running.
- The guest desktop session does not support the expected integration.

Solution:

- Shut down the VM if required by the setting.
- Open VirtualBox VM settings and review General → Advanced → Shared Clipboard.
- Enable the desired clipboard direction.
- Install or configure the appropriate VirtualBox guest integration components according to the official documentation.
- Restart the guest and test with harmless text.

Lesson learned: Clipboard integration requires compatible guest components and correct VM settings.

---

7. File Transfer Between Host and Guest

Problem: Moving files between Windows and Kali Linux is inconvenient or unsuccessful.

Possible causes:

- Shared folders are not configured.
- Guest integration components are missing.
- Folder permissions are incorrect.

Solution:

- Configure a VirtualBox shared folder when appropriate.
- Review folder permissions and access controls.
- Use a dedicated lab transfer folder rather than sharing sensitive host directories.
- Verify transferred files before using them in exercises.

Lesson learned: Controlled file-sharing methods make lab work easier while reducing unnecessary exposure of host files.

---

8. Linux Command-Line Learning Curve

Problem: Basic tasks such as navigating directories, inspecting files, or managing permissions are difficult at first.

Possible causes:

- Limited experience with Linux commands.
- Unfamiliarity with file paths and permissions.
- Confusion between administrator privileges and normal-user access.

Solution:

Practice basic commands:

pwd
ls -la
cd
whoami
id

Learn how to inspect permissions and understand commands before executing them with elevated privileges.

Lesson learned: Consistent command-line practice builds confidence and reduces mistakes during later security exercises.

---

9. Package Updates and Installation Errors

Problem: Installing or updating packages fails.

Possible causes:

- DNS or internet connectivity problems.
- Repository configuration errors.
- Interrupted package operations.
- Insufficient disk space.

Solution:

- Check network connectivity and DNS resolution.
- Review the configured repositories against Kali's official documentation.
- Read the complete error message before changing system settings.
- Use the package manager's standard update workflow and avoid adding untrusted repositories.

Lesson learned: Understanding the error message and checking the underlying cause is better than blindly running commands found online.

---

10. Virtual Machine Security and Isolation

Problem: A lab machine may be exposed to networks or files that were not intended to be part of the exercise.

Possible causes:

- Using Bridged networking unnecessarily.
- Sharing sensitive host folders.
- Running vulnerable targets with unrestricted network access.
- Downloading untrusted files.

Solution:

- Use an isolated virtual network for vulnerable targets.
- Limit shared folders and clipboard integration to what is needed.
- Keep snapshots or clean backups before testing.
- Use intentionally vulnerable applications only in a controlled environment.
- Test only systems you own or have explicit permission to assess.

Lesson learned: A useful security lab should provide practical learning while keeping the host and other networks protected.

---

11. Virtual Machine Snapshots and Recovery

Problem: A configuration change or exercise breaks the VM, making it difficult to return to a working state.

Possible causes:

- No clean baseline was saved.
- Multiple configuration changes were made without testing.
- The VM's state was not backed up.

Solution:

- Create a snapshot after a clean installation and successful basic configuration.
- Take additional snapshots before major experiments.
- Record important changes and test one change at a time.
- Keep separate backups of important documentation.

Lesson learned: Snapshots make experimentation easier to recover from, but they do not replace independent backups of important files.

---

12. Troubleshooting Record Template

Use the following template whenever a new issue occurs.

Issue: [Insert issue title]

- Date:
- Problem encountered:
- Expected behavior:
- Possible cause:
- Troubleshooting steps:
- Solution applied:
- Final result:
- Lesson learned:
- Related screenshot or notes:

---

Conclusion

Building a Kali Linux cybersecurity lab involves more than installing an operating system. It requires understanding virtualization, networking, DNS, Linux administration, and basic security practices.

Documenting each challenge and its resolution creates a repeatable learning process and helps other beginners troubleshoot similar problems.

This document will be updated as the lab grows and more practical exercises are completed.

Disclaimer: This lab is intended for education and authorized security testing only. Never test systems without appropriate permission.

items.title: CI: nightly macOS (Apple Silicon) build that produces an unsigned Koan.dmg
items.body:
Part of #51. Koan ships for **macOS only**; the Linux machine is the agents' compile/test bench. Nothing builds or even compiles the Mac code today, so Mac-only errors (e.g. the Aura include in #54, ⌘T in #58) are found only by review.

## Goal
A GitHub Actions workflow that builds `Koan.app` for macOS arm64 from `develop` and publishes an unsigned `Koan-<version>-<sha>-arm64.dmg` as an artifact (and a rolling `nightly` pre-release).

## Constraints (GitHub-hosted `macos-15`, free for public repos)
- 3 vCPU (M1), 7 GB RAM, 14 GB guaranteed SSD, **6 h per job**.
- A first Chromium build on 3 cores is ~20–40 h, so the build must be **chained across jobs** that carry the build state as an artifact (the approach ungoogled-chromium-macos uses: each job builds ~5h, uploads the build tree, the next resumes; the last packages the .dmg).
- Disk: a full gclient checkout won't fit. Use a source tarball / minimal fetch of the pinned revision (`CHROMIUM_VERSION`), free runner disk space, and trim the out dir between jobs.

## Scope
- `.github/workflows/macos.yml`: schedule (nightly) + `workflow_dispatch` (optionally on a PR ref, for PRs with Mac-specific code).
- Reuse `scripts/build.sh` / `scripts/koan_platform.sh` / `scripts/apply_patches.sh` / `scripts/apply_branding.sh` and the Mac release GN args (`build/koan.gn`, #52) — no separate build logic.
- Package: `.dmg` with `Koan.app`, ad-hoc signed (`codesign -s -`), unsigned for Gatekeeper; document "right-click → Open" / `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine` in docs/USAGE.md.
- Report: build time per job, number of chained jobs, final size.
- Not in scope: notarisation / Developer ID signing, Linux/Windows packaging.

## Done when
A workflow run on `develop` produces a downloadable .dmg whose app launches on an Apple Silicon Mac (verified by the maintainer), and the workflow is documented in CONTRIBUTING / .agent/notes.

items.title: Release QA osquery v5.24.1

labels.name: ~osquery core
labels.description: Relates to a change in osquery core.

items.body:
## Goal | User story | |:---------------------------------------------------------------------------| | As a Fleet user, | I want to use the latest version of osqueryd, | so that I can benefit from new features, bug fixes, and security improvements. Issue to track QA of osquery [5.24.1](https://github.com/osquery/osquery/releases/tag/5.24.1), which is on Fleet's `edge` channel, before it's promoted to `stable`. Release PR: #56949. ## Context 5.24.1 is a patch release on top of 5.24.0 (#55004). The changes that matter to Fleet: - **`IN` constraints in joins (osquery/osquery#9230):** in 5.24.0, when a join reruns for the next outer row, optimized tables (`file`, `hash`) lose the `IN` list and return too few rows, with no error. Reports and policies that join `file` or `hash` with `IN` may have returned incomplete results on 5.24.0. - **eBPF tables restored:** `bpf_process_events` and `bpf_socket_events` were dropped by mistake in 5.24.0 (#56474). - **TLS connection reuse (osquery/osquery#9199):** affects every request to Fleet: enroll, config, distributed read/write, and log shipping. - **Host and instance UUID stability (osquery/osquery#9203):** UUIDs no longer change after every `schedule_reload` with `--disable_database`. - **TLS 1.0/1.1 disabled and CA bundle updated (osquery/osquery#9192, osquery/osquery#9202, osquery/osquery#9206):** osquery requires TLS 1.2 or later, and the eMudhra roots are removed from its bundle. - **Build hardening (osquery/osquery#9167):** `_FORTIFY_SOURCE`, CET/BTI on Linux, and new Windows exploit mitigations. The risk is a startup crash. - **Software inventory tables Fleet reads:** `rpm_packages` (osquery/osquery#9173), `jetbrains_plugins` (osquery/osquery#9223), `prefetch` (osquery/osquery#9211), `chrome_extensions` (osquery/osquery#9177). - **`statfs()` timeout in `mounts` (osquery/osquery#9175):** Fleet's disk space queries read `mounts`. See the full release notes for other changes. ## QA ### Smoke test (Windows, macOS, Linux) - [x] osquery 5.24.1 is on TUF `edge` at updates.fleetdm.com. - [x] Hosts on `edge` upgrade from 5.24.0 to 5.24.1 and stay online. - [x] Live reports, scheduled reports, policies, software inventory, and detail queries all work. - [x] No new errors in osqueryd logs. ### 5.24.1 changes - [x] `IN` joins: this upstream repro returns 4 rows as a live report (5.24.0 returns 2), on each platform with that platform's paths: ```sql SELECT t.n, f.path FROM (SELECT 1 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 2) t CROSS JOIN file f WHERE f.path IN ('/etc/hostname', '/etc/os-release'); ``` - [x] Same for a `hash` variant of the query. - [x] macOS with Firefox and Firefox ESR installed: both show as the correct app (the `macos_firefox` query uses `parse_ini … path IN (SELECT …)`). - [x] Built-in reports and policies that join `file` or `hash` with `IN` return the same rows as before. - [x] eBPF: `bpf_process_events` and `bpf_socket_events` are registered on Linux (#56474). - [x] TLS reuse: live reports, detail query refreshes, scheduled report results and status logs arrive, including behind a load balancer or reverse proxy. - [x] Identity: a host with `--host-identifier=uuid`, and one with `--host-identifier=instance`, keeps its host record across the upgrade and an orbit restart, with no duplicates. - [x] Startup: osqueryd starts and stays up on Windows x64 and arm64, and Linux x86_64 and arm64 (including an older distro). fleetd extension tables return data. - [x] Software: the `rpm_packages` list (including epoch and release) matches 5.24.0; items.title: Add Windows support for disk-space pre-check and other Unix-only packages
items.body:
## Context

PR #471 adds a disk-space pre-check for `build` and `pull` operations that uses `golang.org/x/sys/unix` (`unix.Statfs`). To unblock the PR without delaying the feature on Linux/Darwin, the `diskspace` package is currently limited via `//go:build linux || darwin`, with a no-op stub (`check_other.go`) that keeps non-Unix platforms compiling but skips the check.

This issue tracks the follow-up work to bring **native Windows support** to that pre-check, and incidentally to the rest of the project.

## What's Unix-only today

Cross-compiling the repo (`GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...`) surfaces more than just `diskspace`:

- `pkg/diskspace` — statfs-based available-space check (now stubbed on Windows after #471)
- `pkg/xattr` — `unix.Getxattr` / `unix.Setxattr` for extended attributes
- `pkg/version` — references an undefined `platform` symbol on Windows
- Likely others not yet surveyed

## Proposed Work

1. `pkg/diskspace`: add `check_windows.go` using `windows.GetDiskFreeSpaceEx` (from `golang.org/x/sys/windows`) instead of statfs; drop the stub once this lands
2. `pkg/xattr`: decide whether xattrs make sense on Windows (NTFS alternate data streams?) or explicitly document the limitation
3. `pkg/version`: fix the undefined `platform` reference on non-Unix builds
4. Add a CI job that runs `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` to prevent regressions

## References

- PR #471 (disk-space pre-check, currently Unix-only)
- Gemini review flagged the portability concern twice, escalating to HIGH severity

items.title: Excessive disk space usage
items.body:
When installing HIE from the AUR on Arch Linux, the build process generates many build artifacts that are not included in the package in the `~/.stack` directory.

Even when HIE is installed only for the system's own GHC version, the directory is almost 5 GB in size, which includes two seemingly redundant copies of GHC (the same verison of GHC as I already have installed) and a sqlite database which is itself over 700 megabytes in size.

This makes this package one of the largest packages on my system and makes it difficult to justify using HIE, as I only have 256 GB of storage (not an unusual amount now that many laptops come with only an SSD), not all of which is available to Arch because of my Windows dual-boot, and I imagine I am far from the only one in a situation like this.

Would it be possible to use the system-provided GHC, or at least prune some of this disk space after building the package?

items.title: [TUTORIAL] How to run on linux
items.body: WORKING ON Steam Deck, CachyOS, PopOS and UBUNTU ### I RECOMMEND USING PROTON 10, people told me that they had problems running the script using proton 11 and experimental (you can try run and fix yourself tho :P) --- ## Setup (u might not even need to do this, tbh) **i recommend you to extract the .iso and point to the extracted folder instead of the .iso (some people said that they didnt needed but i needed)** use extractxiso to extract [https://github.com/XboxDev/extract-xiso/releases/download/build-202609111233/extract-xiso_Linux.zip](https://github.com/XboxDev/extract-xiso/releases/download/build-202609111233/extract-xiso_Linux.zip) how to use extractXiso --- ## THE SCRIPT! this is the linux script to run the game: [play.sh](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34277456/play.sh) --- ## Three ways to play **`./play.sh`** - plain play. On first run it automatically asks you to point to your game files, installs tools, extracts the game, compiles, and starts playing. **`./play.sh --launcher`** - opens **Start Here**, the little launcher: set your name (gamertag), choose the game folder, see reports, **Play TTT2**, **Play BlueSpark** and the **Update** button. No terminal prompts: the launcher's own Choose/Install buttons do the setup. **`./play.sh --bluespark`** - plays through the **BlueSpark fast client** (the client opens and starts the game hidden behind it). The game needs to be built/installed first. BlueSpark on Wine/Proton: the client needs `icuuc.dll`, but recent Proton ships only the merged `icu.dll`, so the client used to exit at once with `0xC0000135` (DLL not found). `play.sh` now fixes that automatically (copies `icu.dll` as `fastclient/bin/icuuc.dll`). Nothing for you to do - same workaround used by other QT6 apps --- ## Updating Easiest: run `./play.sh --launcher` and press **Update** in Start Here. Under Wine the package signature check is skipped in this mode (Wine has no ECC P-256), so Update can actually run; the SHA-256, zip-slip and package-info checks still run, and the current build is kept if anything fails. Old way: throw the new launcher/package files on the folder and overwrite, then run: `./play.sh --rebuild` --- set the profile name (gamertag) using: `./play.sh --name NAME` if you have less than 1 GB in your root dir run: `./play.sh --skip-space-check` https://github.com/avim2/BlueSpark/issues/6#issuecomment-6509215286 --- ## All options ``` ./play.sh play (automatic setup on first run) ./play.sh --launcher open Start Here (name, icon, reports, Play TTT2 / Play BlueSpark) ./play.sh --bluespark play through the BlueSpark client (fast client) ./play.sh --offline play without online ./play.sh --name NAME set the profile name (gamertag) ./play.sh --rebuild recompile the game (the build step) ./play.sh --window 1920x1080 window instead of fullscreen ./play.sh --dev developer overlays (F4 = settings with resolution) ./play.sh --switch=VAL extra game switch (e.g. --switch=--log_level=debug) ./play.sh --choose-proton pick which Proton to use (saved in proton.conf) ./play.sh --proton=PATH use this Proton for this run only ./play.sh --files ISO_OR_DIR --update TU_FILE prepare the game files manually ./play.sh --game-folder DIR point at an existing folder with default.xex ./play.sh --install-tools download compiler tools manually (~1.3 GB) ./play.sh --status show what is done: tools, game files, build ./play.sh --skip-space-check skip the disk-space check for this run ``` --- ### TROUBLESHOOTING: problem: ``` CMake Generate step failed. Build files cannot be regenerated correctly. Exception: Z:\home\chrischros\Dokumente\Tekken Tag 2 Recomp\ttt2-playtest-release10-268df2b\ttt2-playtest\rex\build-windows.ps1:54 Line | 54 | . XITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Failed ( L A S T E X I T C O D E ) : ($args -join ' ')" } | ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ | Failed (1): cmake --preset win-amd64-release | -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=Z:\home\chrischros\Dokumente\Tekken Tag 2 | Recomp\ttt2-playtest-release10-268df2b\ttt2-playtest\rex\prebuilt\sdk | -DCMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_CONFIGURATION=Release -DTTT2_PREBUILT=ON | -DTTT2_OURS_LIB=OFF ``` fix: https://github.com/avim2/BlueSpark/issues/6#issuecomment-6456377581 --- SCRIPT: ```bash #!/bin/bash # play.sh - play TTT2 Native on Linux through Proton # # Usage: # ./play.sh play (automatic setup on first run) # ./play.sh --offline play without online # ./play.sh --name NAME set the profile name (gamertag) # ./play.sh --rebuild recompile the game (the build step) # ./play.sh --window 1920x1080 window instead of fullscreen # ./play.sh --dev developer overlays (F4 = settings with resolution) # ./play.sh --switch=VAL extra game switch (e.g. --switch=--log_level=debug) # ./play.sh --choose-proton pick which Proton to use (saved in proton.conf) # ./play.sh --proton=PATH use this Proton for this run only # ./play.sh --files ISO_OR_DIR do [ -z "$a" ] && continue EXTRAWIN+=" \"$a\"" done [ "$DEV" = 1 ] && EXTRAWIN+=" \"--ttt2_dev_overlays=true\"" fi # Compatibility runner for Wine / Proton: # 1. Mocks Get-CimInstance because Wine does not implement the native CIM/WMI infrastructure (avoids TypeInitializationException) # 2. Sets TTT2_TOOLCHAIN_TEST_NO_TAR=1 so toolchain.ps1 unpacks archives with portable Python instead of looking for Windows System32/tar.exe # 3. Direct codegen & directory creation so Ninja does not fail on CMake 3.31 depfiles under Wine RUNNER_PS1="$TMPD/runner.ps1" cat > "$RUNNER_PS1" <<'EOF' function global:Get-CimInstance { param( [string]$ClassName, [string]$Filter, [string]$Namespace, $ErrorAction ) if ($ClassName -eq 'Win32_Process') { try { return @(Get-Process -Name 'tar', 'python', 'pythonw' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { [PSCustomObject]@{ ProcessId = $_.Id; CommandLine = ''; Name = $_.ProcessName } }) } catch { return @() } } return @() } $env:TTT2_TOOLCHAIN_TEST_NO_TAR = '1' $targetScript = $args[0] $targetArgs = @($args | Select-Object -Skip 1) try { $scriptDir = Split-Path -Parent $targetScript $root = if (Test-Path (Join-Path $scriptDir 'setup-steps.ps1')) { Split-Path -Parent $scriptDir } else { $scriptDir } $rexDir = Join-Path $root 'rex' $buildDir = Join-Path $rexDir 'out\build\win-amd64-release' $rexglueExe = Join-Path $rexDir 'prebuilt\sdk\bin\rexglue.exe' $manifest = Join-Path $rexDir 'ttt2_manifest.toml' $sourcesCmake = Join-Path $rexDir 'generated\default\sources.cmake' $defaultTu = Join-Path $root 'gamedata\default_tu.xex' New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force (Join-Path $buildDir 'CMakeFiles\d') -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force (Join-Path $rexDir 'generated\default') -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null $isBuild = $false for ($i = 0; $i -lt $targetArgs.Count; $i++) { if ($targetArgs[$i] -eq 'build' -or $targetArgs[$i] -eq '-Step' -and ($i + 1 -lt $targetArgs.Count -and $targetArgs[$i+1] -eq 'build')) { $isBuild = $true break } } if ($isBuild) { if ((Test-Path $rexglueExe) -and (Test-Path $manifest) -and (Test-Path $defaultTu) -and -not (Test-Path $sourcesCmake)) { Write-Host '== Recompiling the game code from gamedata\default_tu.xex (standalone)' -ForegroundColor Cyan Push-Location $rexDir try { & $rexglueExe codegen $manifest } finally { Pop-Location } } } } catch { } & $targetScript @targetArgs if ($null -ne $LASTEXITCODE) { exit $LASTEXITCODE } EOF # The patched space check skips only while TTT2_NO_SPACE_CHECK=1. Set it where the # steps actually run: the runner starts them in this same pwsh process # (`& $targetScript`), which is how play.sh already passes TTT2_TOOLCHAIN_TEST_NO_TAR. if [ "$SPACE_ON" = 1 ]; then printf '%s\n' "\$env:TTT2_NO_SPACE_CHECK = '1'" >> "$RUNNER_PS1" fi if [ "$SIG_ON" = 1 ]; then printf '%s\n' "\$env:TTT2_NO_SIG_CHECK = '1'" >> "$RUNNER_PS1" fi RUNNER_WIN="Z:$(printf '%s' "$RUNNER_PS1" | sed 's|/|\\|g')" # Build commands list CMDS=() if [ "$AUTO_TOOLS" = 1 ] || [ "$STEP" = tools ] || [ "$TOOLS_BEFORE" = 1 ]; then CMDS+=("\"$PWSH\" -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \"$RUNNER_WIN\" \"$PSWIN\" -Step tools -AcceptMicrosoftLicense") fi if [ "$AUTO_FILES" = 1 ] || [ "$STEP" = files ]; then CMDS+=("\"$PWSH\" -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \"$RUNNER_WIN\" \"$FILESWIN\"") fi if [ "$AUTO_BUILD" = 1 ] || [ "$STEP" = build ]; then CMDS+=("\"$PWSH\" -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \"$RUNNER_WIN\" \"$PSWIN\" -Step build") fi LAUNCHERWIN="Z:$(printf '%s' "$DIR/rex/launcher.ps1" | sed 's|/|\\|g')" if [ "$LAUNCH_MODE" = launcher ]; then CMDS+=("\"$PWSH\" -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \"$RUNNER_WIN\" \"$LAUNCHERWIN\"") elif [ "$LAUNCH_MODE" = bluespark ]; then # Play's own switch list first, then the client (it starts the game behind it) CMDS+=("\"$PWSH\" -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \"$RUNNER_WIN\" \"$PSWIN\" -Step switches$ARGSWIN") FASTCLIENT_WIN="Z:$(printf '%s' "$FASTCLIENT_LIN" | sed 's|/|\\|g')" FASTCLIENT_DIR="Z:$(printf '%s' "$DIR/fastclient/bin" | sed 's|/|\\|g')" CMDS+=("cd /d \"$FASTCLIENT_DIR\" && \"$FASTCLIENT_WIN\"") fi if [ "$STEP" = play ] && [ "$LAUNCH_MODE" = play ]; then if [ -n "$DEVWIN" ]; then CMDS+=("\"$PWSH\" -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \"$RUNNER_WIN\" \"$PSWIN\" -Step switches$ARGSWIN") CMDS+=("\"$PWSH\" -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \"$RUNNER_WIN\" \"$DEVWIN\" \"$REXWIN\"$EXTRAWIN") else CMDS+=("\"$PWSH\" -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \"$RUNNER_WIN\" \"$PSWIN\" -Step play$ARGSWIN") fi elif [ "$STEP" = status ]; then CMDS+=("\"$PWSH\" -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \"$RUNNER_WIN\" \"$PSWIN\" -Step status") fi { echo '@echo off' if [ "$LAUNCH_MODE" = launcher ]; then echo 'set "PATH=C:\PowerShell7;%PATH%"' # Start Here shows its steps' output in a text box, and PowerShell 7 colors errors # with ANSI escapes that the box shows raw: TERM=dumb keeps them plain text. echo 'set "TERM=dumb"' fi n=${#CMDS[@]} i=0 for c in "${CMDS[@]}"; do i=$((i + 1)) if [ "$i" -eq 1 ]; then echo "$c > \"$LOG_WIN\" 2>&1" else echo "$c >> \"$LOG_WIN\" 2>&1" fi echo "set RC=%ERRORLEVEL%" if [ "$i" -lt "$n" ]; then echo "if not %RC%==0 goto :done" fi done echo ':done' echo "echo. >> \"$LOG_WIN\"" echo "echo [play.sh] exit=%RC% >> \"$LOG_WIN\"" } > "$BAT" rm -f "$LOG_LIN" touch "$LOG_LIN" # The temporary patch goes on right before the steps run (restored on exit) if [ "$SPACE_ON" = 1 ]; then space_patch || true; fi if [ "$SIG_ON" = 1 ]; then sig_patch || true; fi # Run Proton in the background and stream log output to terminal in real time "$PROTON/proton" run cmd.exe /c "$BAT_WIN" & PROTON_PID=$! tail -n +1 -f --pid="$PROTON_PID" "$LOG_LIN" 2>/dev/null & TAIL_PID=$! wait "$PROTON_PID" || true kill "$TAIL_PID" 2>/dev/null || true space_restore sig_restore echo if [ -f "$LOG_LIN" ]; then rc=$(sed -n 's/^\[play.sh\] exit=//p' "$LOG_LIN" | tr -d '\r' | tail -1) exit "${rc:-0}" else echo "error: the game never started (no log was written)." >&2 exit 1 fi ```

items.title: ci: stabilize MinGW installation for Ubuntu Windows GNU cross-compile gate
items.body:
## Observed failure (2026-10-27 UTC)

The [main CI run 40519444890](https://github.com/genm/rackio/actions/runs/40519444890) at commit [`c7a19be6`](https://github.com/genm/rackio/commit/c7a19be6ad1a741d9f6b195061dea7f37ddbf326) failed only the **Rust Windows cross-compile check** job ([job logs](https://github.com/genm/rackio/actions/runs/40519444890/job/122242273294)). Linux/macOS/Windows Rust matrix, frontend, dependency policy, CodeQL and Security passed.

Failure happened **before Cargo compilation**, while installing `mingw-w64` on the Ubuntu 24.04 cross-compile runner:

- `apt-get update/install of mingw-w64 failed after 3 attempts` (job exit 1).
- `mingw-w64` metapackage pulls 25 packages and ~269 MB of archives; log reports ~1.3 GB of extra disk space.
- The workflow wraps install in `timeout 120s`; archive fetches are slow/stall, including `azure.archive.ubuntu.com`. Retries/backoff did not recover.
- This is a **CI tool provisioning failure**, *not* evidence that Windows-target Rust sources fail to compile. A transient mirror issue is possible; diagnose before changing test coverage.

## Action

1. Reproduce on a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 GitHub runner; record apt timing, failing URL and exit reason. Do not classify a single run as an application regression.
2. Reduce/robustify provisioning: evaluate target-specific `gcc-mingw-w64-x86-64` packages instead of the full `mingw-w64` metapackage, an available preinstalled toolchain, an alternate apt mirror, and/or appropriate timeouts. Keep supply-chain pinning and avoid masking failures.
3. Retain the `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` Rust check/Clippy gate, including `rackio-windows-ipc`; **do not convert failure to skipped/continue-on-error**.
4. Verify green cross-compilation (not just successful apt install) on fresh runners, and preserve logs/evidence in CI.

This is distinct from [Issue #220](https://github.com/genm/rackio/issues/220), which addresses redundant Cargo check/Clippy work *after* provisioning succeeds.

## Follow-up (2026-10-29 UTC)

- The later [main CI run 40802667658](https://github.com/genm/rackio/actions/runs/40802667658) on [`08e7787`](https://github.com/genm/rackio/commit/08e7787a7a83c84c966c24c63e8023e7f07e6cf6) completed successfully, **including the Rust Windows cross-compile check**. [Security](https://github.com/genm/rackio/actions/runs/40802667805) and [CodeQL](https://github.com/genm/rackio/actions/runs/40802667694) also passed.
- This is evidence of recovery on that runner, not proof that `mingw-w64` package provisioning is reliable. Keep the issue open until repeated fresh-run evidence or a documented provisioning hardening decision.

items.title: API to Auto-Resolve Disk Space Errors on Linux Servers
items.body:
Create an API that can automatically detect and resolve disk space errors on Linux-based servers.

Requirements:
- The API should scan for common disk space issues (e.g., low available space, large log files, orphaned temp files).
- Implement automatic remediation steps such as cleaning up log files, removing unused packages, and alerting if manual intervention is required.
- The solution should be extensible for future file system issues.
- Provide endpoints for triggering scans and remediations on-demand.
- Include robust logging and error reporting.

Notes:
- Target platform: Linux servers
- Disk space errors are the initial focus; future enhancements may include other file system issues.
- No repository specified yet.

items.title: Docs: "Removing MySQL with APT" leaves server running and repo enabled; no Yum section
items.body:
### MySQL version / commit

Reference Manual 8.4/9.7/26.7 and APT quick guide:
- https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/9.7/en/linux-installation-apt-repo.html ("Removing MySQL with APT")
- https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/9.7/en/linux-installation-yum-repo.html and linux-installation-rpm.html (no removal section)

Tested with 26.7.0-1debian13 (APT) and 26.7.0-1.el9 (Yum).

### Steps to reproduce

APT (Debian 13):

```
sudo apt-get remove mysql-server
systemctl is-active mysql
sudo apt-get autoremove
```

Then install 8.4.10 from the DEB bundle as described on linux-installation-debian (`dpkg -i ...`, `sudo apt-get -f install`).

### Expected vs actual result

Docs: "`sudo apt-get remove mysql-server`" ... "Then, remove any other software that was installed automatically with the MySQL server: `sudo apt-get autoremove`".

Actual: `apt-get remove mysql-server` removes only the metapackage and the server keeps running:

```
The following packages will be REMOVED:
  mysql-server
After this operation, 70.7 kB disk space will be freed.
Removing mysql-server (26.7.0-1debian13) ...
active
```

`apt-get autoremove` then removes the rest and stops the server. Left behind: `/var/lib/mysql`, `/etc/mysql`, `/var/log/mysql`, packages in state `rc`, the debconf answers (the next install does not ask for a root password), and `mysql-apt-config` with `mysql-innovation` still enabled.

Because the repository is still enabled, the later DEB-bundle install of 8.4.10 was turned into 26.7.0 by `apt-get -f install`:

```
The following packages will be upgraded:
  mysql-client mysql-common mysql-community-client mysql-community-client-core
  mysql-community-client-plugins mysql-community-server
  mysql-community-server-core mysql-server
```

and the server started on the old 26.7 data directory. `apt-get purge mysql-community-server` asks "Remove data directories ?", which the page does not mention.

Yum/RPM: there is no removal section. `sudo dnf remove 'mysql-community-*' mysql-shell mysql97-community-release` works but leaves `/var/lib/mysql`, `/var/log/mysqld.log`, the imported keys and the `mysql` user. A later "fresh" 9.7.1 install then fails to start: `Cannot downgrade from 260700 to 90701`.

### Platform / compiler

Debian 13 (trixie), Ubuntu 24.04 (APT); Rocky Linux 9.8 (Yum/RPM); x86_64.

### Suggested fix

APT section:
> To remove MySQL completely: `sudo systemctl stop mysql`; `sudo apt-get purge mysql-server mysql-community-server mysql-community-server-core mysql-client mysql-community-client mysql-community-client-core mysql-community-client-plugins mysql-common`; `sudo apt-get autoremove --purge`. Purging asks whether to delete the data directory. To stop using the MySQL APT repository: `sudo apt-get purge mysql-apt-config && sudo apt-get update`.

linux-installation-debian: "If the MySQL APT repository is configured, remove it first, or `apt-get -f install` may replace the downloaded packages with the repository's version."

New Yum/RPM section:
> `sudo systemctl stop mysqld; sudo dnf remove 'mysql-community-*' 'mysql*-community-release'`. `/var/lib/mysql`, `/var/log/mysqld.log` and `/var/lib/mysql-files` are not removed; move them aside before installing a different (lower) series: `sudo mv /var/lib/mysql /var/lib/mysql.old`.

Found during a hands-on validation of the install/upgrade documentation on 2026-10-10 (Percona).

items.title: [Package]: Premake
items.body:
### Why is it worth to add this package?

### What it is?
**Premake** is an open-source command-line tool designed to **automate and simplify the creation of build systems** for software projects.

In simple terms, it allows you to describe your project’s build rules just once and, from there, automatically generate the files needed to build that project across various IDEs, operating systems, and tools.

### How does it work?
Your project’s configuration is written in a script file using the **Lua** language (usually named `premake5.lua`). Lua is a lightweight, fast, and easy-to-learn language. You use this script to define things like:
* Where your source code files are located.
* Which libraries need to be linked.
* Which directories should be included (*include directories*).
* What the build types are (Debug, Release, etc.).

After writing the script, you run the Premake command in the terminal to generate the files for your specific environment. For example:
* `premake5 vs2022` generates a **Visual Studio** solution on Windows.
* `premake5 xcode4` generates an **Xcode** project for macOS.
* `premake5 gmake2` generates **GNU Makefiles** for compiling on Linux.

### Why does this matter?
Various projects have their own build system. **Premake** becomes a required dependency for building these projects. This can also be used by future packages added to the Termux ecosystem. 

### Home page URL

https://premake.github.io/

### Source code URL

https://github.com/premake/premake-core

### Packaging policy acknowledgement

- [x] The project is actively developed.
- [x] The project has [existing packages](https://repology.org/projects/) and is "well known".
- [x] Licensed under an [open source license](https://spdx.org/licenses/).
- [x] Not available through a language package manager: cargo, cpan, dotnet tool, gem, npm, pip, etc.

- [x] Not taking up too much disk space (< 100MiB per architecture, exceptions can be made)
- [x] Not duplicating the functionality of existing packages.
- [x] Not serving hacking, malware, phishing, spamming, spying, ddos functionality.
- [x] I certify that I have read [Termux Packaging Policy](https://github.com/termux/termux-packages/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#packaging-policy) and understand that my request will be denied if it is found lacking.

items.title: Remote servers: open a live dashboard of a server's CPU, memory and disk usage, with statistics since the server started
items.body:
## Summary

Add a **Dashboard** button for each server in the Environments sidebar and in Settings → Remote Servers. It opens a panel that shows the host the server runs on:

- total CPU usage, as a percentage of all cores;
- memory used and total;
- used and free space for each disk or volume.

The values update in real time. Each measure also shows statistics since the server process started: current, minimum, average, maximum and p95, with a small chart. The dashboard works on Linux, macOS and Windows servers, and for the local environment as well as remote ones.

Today BiBCode measures only its own processes. It collects nothing about the whole host, and it reads no disk space at all.

## Current behavior (verified at `fd98b433068b`, main, 2026-11-02)

**Server: what is measured today**
- `sysinfo` 0.39.6 is already a workspace dependency (`Cargo.toml:86`, `apps/server/Cargo.toml:65`). [code]
- Its only uses are per-process: liveness checks (`apps/server/src/process/liveness.rs:5`) and the native process sampler (`apps/server/src/diagnostics/native.rs:7`). Nothing calls `global_cpu_usage`, `total_memory`, `available_memory` or `Disks`. [verified: `rg` over `apps/server/src` and `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src`]
- `DiagnosticsMonitor` (`apps/server/src/diagnostics/monitor.rs`) samples BiBCode's own process tree on demand. It is built with a 2 s interval (`apps/server/src/production/runtime.rs:597-600`), stops after three intervals without a reader (`monitor.rs:24-26`, "a server nobody reads samples nothing"), and hides the OS behind a fakeable `ProcessSampler` trait (`monitor.rs:37`). [code]
- Its history is kept in memory for one hour, with at most 20,000 samples (`apps/server/src/diagnostics/history.rs:12-13`). [code]

**Protocol**
- The per-process data reaches clients through two unary RPCs, `server.getProcessDiagnostics` and `server.getProcessResourceHistory` (`apps/server/src/rpc/methods.rs:167-168`, scope `SCOPE_ORCHESTRATION_READ` at `apps/server/src/auth/scope.rs:66-67`, registered at `apps/server/src/production/server_terminal.rs:592-613`). Clients poll them. [code]
- Streaming RPCs already exist: `read_stream(...)` in `apps/server/src/rpc/methods.rs:40` and contract entries with `stream: true` (for example `packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts:856`). `server_terminal.rs:557-590` shows a stream loop that sends on an interval and stops on `sender.closed()`. [code]
- Remote connections carry all RPCs over one authenticated WebSocket, encrypted end to end with Noise on direct connections (`docs/architecture/remote.md:203-216`). A new stream needs no new transport. [code]
- The server advertises features as capability flags that decode to `false` when missing (`packages/contracts/src/environment.ts:66-90`, for example `diagnosticLogs` at `:84`). Both descriptors set them: `apps/server/src/lifecycle.rs:73` and `apps/server/src/production/control.rs:2728`. The descriptor also carries `platform` and `bootId` (`lifecycle.rs:52`, `:58`). [code]

**Web**
- The Environments sidebar view renders `SidebarEnvironmentContextCard` (`apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:375`, `:5519`). Its "Environment actions" menu (`apps/web/src/components/sidebar/EnvironmentContextCard.tsx:138-165`) has Disconnect, Show update steps, Check for updates and Manage…. [code]
- Settings → Remote Servers lists each saved server as a `RemoteServerRow` (`apps/web/src/components/settings/remote-servers/ConnectTab.tsx:171`) with Check (`:436`) and Connect/Disconnect (`:481`) buttons. [code]
- The status bar shows BiBCode's own CPU and memory (`apps/web/src/components/status-bar/ResourceUsageSegment.tsx`) by polling every 2 s (`apps/web/src/components/status-bar/AppStatusBar.tsx:47`). Settings → Diagnostics shows the process history for 5 m to 1 h windows (`apps/web/src/components/settings/resourceDiagnosticsPresentation.ts:71-74`) with a bar chart (`apps/web/src/components/settings/ResourceDiagnosticsSections.tsx:440`). [code]

**Lessons from earlier issues**
- #24: a host-wide `System::new_all()` scan on every boot cost real CPU. #232: idle terminals scanned the host process table every second. The new collector must not walk the process table. [verified: issue text]
- #168: an unfocused window polled diagnostics every 2 s all night, about 11.5 MB/h into the webview. Live updates must stop when nobody is looking. [verified: issue text]

## Prior art

- **T3 Code** (`pingdotgg/t3code` at `115739c1e02e`) reads host CPU and memory in `apps/server/src/resourceTelemetry/HostResources.ts`. CPU is two readings 200 ms apart (`:47`). Available memory comes from `MemAvailable` on Linux (`:62`) and `vm_stat` on macOS (`:66`). Reads are cached for 5 s (`:85`). `docs/internals/resource-telemetry.md:11-21` samples on a timer only while a subscriber is live, keeps bounded in-memory history, and has "no telemetry database". No disk space. [verified]
- **Orca** (`stablyai/orca` at `a38acbe3546d`) defines `HostMemory` with total, free, available and used, and records where "available" came from (`src/shared/process-stats-types.ts:24`, `:52-58`). No disk space found. [verified]
- `sysinfo` 0.39.6 gives everything needed: `System::refresh_cpu_usage` and `global_cpu_usage` (`src/common/system.rs:193`, `:501`), `total_memory` and `available_memory` (`:539`, `:575`), and `Disks` with `mount_point`, `file_system`, `total_space`, `available_space`, `is_removable` and `is_read_only` (`src/common/disk.rs:63-133`). CPU usage is a difference between two refreshes at least `MINIMUM_CPU_UPDATE_INTERVAL` apart, 200 ms on Linux, macOS and Windows. On Linux it already skips pseudo filesystems, `tmpfs`, and NFS/CIFS/autofs mounts, because `statvfs` "may hang" on hard network mounts (`src/unix/linux/disk.rs:401-428`). It does not skip `overlay`. Windows reports no separate "available" memory (`src/common/system.rs:566`). [verified: crate source]

## Proposal

### Server

1. Add a `HostMetricsCollector` in `apps/server/src/diagnostics/`. It reads through a `HostMetricsSource` trait so tests can fake it, the same way `ProcessSampler` works. The native source keeps one `System::new()` (never `new_all()`) and one `Disks` list. It refreshes only CPU usage, memory and disk space. It never touches processes.
2. One sample holds:
   - `sampledAt`;
   - `cpuPercent` (0 to 100, all cores together) and `cpuCount`;
   - `memoryTotalBytes`, `memoryUsedBytes` (total minus available), `memoryAvailableBytes`;
   - `disks`: for each volume, `mountPoint`, `name`, `fileSystem`, `totalBytes`, `freeBytes` (available to the server's user), `usedBytes` (total minus free), `removable`, `readOnly`.
3. Filter volumes on every platform. Keep sysinfo's Linux filter. Also skip `overlay`, `squashfs` and zero-size volumes. On macOS show one entry for each APFS container, so `/` and `/System/Volumes/Data` do not appear twice. [inferred: confirm on a real Mac] Show removable volumes, marked as removable.
4. Read disks on a blocking thread with a time limit (for example 2 s). A volume that does not answer in time shows as "Not responding" and does not delay CPU and memory.
5. Sampling runs at two rates:
   - **Background**: every 60 s from server start, so the statistics cover the whole uptime. One sample reads `/proc/stat` and `/proc/meminfo` (or the macOS and Windows equivalents) plus one free-space call per volume. Disk space can be read every fifth background sample.
   - **Live**: every 1 s while at least one dashboard stream is open. The collector drops back to background rate when the last stream closes, as `DiagnosticsMonitor` does.
6. Keep the statistics in memory, from the server start (`bootId`):
   - For each measure (CPU %, memory %, and used % per disk): count, sum, minimum, maximum, current, and a fixed 1-point-percentage histogram (101 bins) for p95. This stays a fixed size however long the server runs.
   - Chart history in tiers: the last 15 minutes at full live resolution, the last 24 hours at 1-minute averages, and older data at 15-minute averages. Each tier keeps average and peak, as `ProcessResourceHistory` buckets do. Cap the total memory (for example 1 MiB) and coarsen the oldest tier when the cap is reached.
7. Add a stream RPC `server.subscribeHostMetrics` (`read_stream`, scope `SCOPE_ORCHESTRATION_READ`). The first message is a snapshot: host facts (OS, arch, host CPU count, total memory), `startedAt`, `bootId`, the current sample, statistics and chart history. Each later message carries one live sample and the updated statistics. The stream ends when the client closes it.
8. Add a capability flag `hostMetrics` in `packages/contracts/src/environment.ts` and set it in both descriptors (`lifecycle.rs`, `production/control.rs`).
9. Expose the same snapshot as a read-only MCP diagnostics tool next to the existing ones (`apps/server/src/mcp/tools/diagnostics.rs:75-76`). [P2]

### Web

1. Add a **Dashboard** item to the "Environment actions" menu in `EnvironmentContextCard`, and a **Dashboard** button in each connected `RemoteServerRow`. The local environment gets the same item.
2. The dashboard opens as a sheet (`apps/web/src/components/ui/sheet.tsx`) titled with the environment name. It shows:
   - **CPU**: a large current percentage, the core count, and a live chart.
   - **Memory**: used of total (for example "11.2 GB of 32 GB, 35%") and a live chart.
   - **Disks**: one row per volume with a usage bar, "used of total" and "free". Removable and read-only volumes get a badge.
   - **Since server start**: "Since <time> (up <duration>)" with current, min, avg, p95 and max for each measure, plus a chart of the whole uptime.
3. Subscribe only while the sheet is open and the window is visible. Close the stream when the sheet closes or the document is hidden. Reopen it on return (#168).
4. States:
   - **Loading**: skeletons until the first snapshot.
   - **Live**: values update every second.
   - **Stale**: no message for 3 s. Values dim and show "Last updated <n> s ago".
   - **Disconnected**: the environment is not connected. The sheet keeps the last values, dimmed, with "Disconnected". It resubscribes after reconnect.
   - **Restarted**: after reconnect, a different `bootId` means the server restarted. The statistics reset, and a note says "Server restarted at <time>".
   - **Unsupported**: `capabilities.hostMetrics` is false. The button stays visible and the sheet says "This server's version doesn't report host metrics. Update it to see this dashboard." with the existing update action. The client never sends the RPC to such a server.
   - **Error**: the stream failed. Show the message and a Retry button.
5. Format values with the existing helpers `formatMemoryBytes` and `formatCpuPercent` (`apps/web/src/components/status-bar/statusBarFormat.ts:72`, `:86`). Follow `UI.md` sizes and spacing. No em dashes in UI copy (#222).

## Goals

- See the load of any connected server in one click, without opening a terminal on it.
- The same numbers and layout on Linux, macOS and Windows hosts.
- Near-zero cost when no dashboard is open.

## Non-goals

- Per-process lists, per-core charts, network, GPU, swap, temperatures or battery.
- Alerts, thresholds or notifications.
- History that survives a server restart (see open question 1).
- Exporting metrics (OTLP, Prometheus).
- Changes to the existing BiBCode process diagnostics, status bar or profiler.

## Requirements

### P0

1. **Collector.** CPU, memory and disk readings through a fakeable source, with no process scan.
   - Test: Rust unit tests with a fake source cover used = total minus available, `cpuPercent` limited to 0..100, the volume filter (`overlay`, `squashfs`, zero-size and duplicate entries removed), and a volume that times out showing as not responding while CPU and memory still arrive.
2. **Statistics.** Min, avg, max, current and p95 since start, at a fixed size.
   - Test: with a fake source and a paused clock (as in `monitor.rs` tests), feeding known values gives exact min, avg, max and the p95 bin. One week of simulated background samples keeps the history under the cap and keeps the first sample's time as the start.
3. **Two sampling rates.** 60 s in the background, 1 s while a stream is open, back to 60 s after the last stream closes.
   - Test: paused-clock test that counts source reads with zero, one and two subscribers, and after both leave.
4. **Stream RPC and scope.** `server.subscribeHostMetrics` with a snapshot first and then samples. It requires `SCOPE_ORCHESTRATION_READ`.
   - Test: `every_active_rpc_method_has_exactly_one_declared_scope` (`apps/server/src/auth/scope.rs:244`) passes with the new method. A server terminal RPC test shows that an unauthenticated or under-scoped session is refused, and that the stream ends when the client closes.
5. **Contract.** Effect schemas in `packages/contracts/src/server.ts` and `rpc.ts`, the `hostMetrics` capability defaulting to `false`.
   - Test: a Rust contract fixture exported by `packages/contracts/scripts/export-rust-rpc-fixtures.ts`, decoded by a Rust test, as done for `server__getProcessResourceHistory-success.json`. A descriptor without `hostMetrics` decodes to `false`. Both descriptor tests assert `hostMetrics` is `true` (next to `lifecycle.rs:1290` and `control.rs:6976`).
6. **Entry points.** The Dashboard item in the environment menu and the button in each connected remote server row.
   - Test: web tests render both and open the sheet for the right environment.
7. **Dashboard states.** Loading, live, stale, disconnected, restarted, unsupported and error, as described above.
   - Test: one web test per state with a fake stream. The unsupported test asserts that no RPC is sent.
8. **Stop when hidden.** The stream is closed when the sheet closes or the document is hidden.
   - Test: a web test that hides the document and asserts the subscription ended.
9. **Cross-platform build.** The collector compiles and its tests pass on the Linux, macOS and Windows CI runners.

### P1

1. Charts for CPU and memory over the last 15 minutes, and for the whole uptime, with average and peak per bucket.
2. A setting to show volumes hidden by the default filter, and to hide removable volumes.
3. A live check on a real Linux, macOS and Windows host, recorded in the PR: the numbers match `top`/`free`/`df`, Activity Monitor and Disk Utility, and Task Manager within a few percent.
4. A measured cost: background sampling under 0.1% of one core, and a live 1 s stream under 1%. Measure on the maintainer's dev host and record the method. [guess: targets to confirm]

### P2

1. The MCP diagnostics tool for the host snapshot.
2. Per-disk statistics in the "Since server start" section, not only the current value.

## Gates

`vp run test`, `vp check`, `vp run typecheck`, the Rust tests for `apps/server`, and the React best-practices and `UI.md` reviews for the new web components.

## Open questions

1. **What does "since BiBCode launched" cover?**
   - (a) Since this server process started. Memory only, reset on every restart or update.
   - (b) Across restarts. Persist the downsampled tiers to SQLite (for example one row per 15-minute bucket, kept for 90 days) and show "Since <first sample>".
   - Recommendation: (a) first, which is what this issue specifies. It needs no schema change or migration. Add (b) as a follow-up if the maintainer wants history across updates. The sheet already shows the start time, so the meaning is clear to the user.
2. **Background sampling from boot.** The statistics need a sampler that runs while nobody watches, unlike `DiagnosticsMonitor`. Recommendation: allow it at 60 s with no process scan, and gate it behind a setting only if the measured cost (P1.4) says so.
3. **Which volumes count as "all disks"?** Recommendation: local fixed and removable volumes. Skip network mounts by default on every platform, because a hung mount can block a read. Let the P1 setting add them.
4. **Scope.** Mount points can reveal paths. Recommendation: `SCOPE_ORCHESTRATION_READ`, the same as `server.getProcessDiagnostics`, which already exposes process command lines.
5. **Where the sheet lives.** A sheet keeps the user's place in the sidebar. Recommendation: a sheet, with an "Open in Settings" link added later if a full page is wanted.

## Duplicate check

Searched open and closed issues and PRs in mubeda/BibCode for: dashboard, metrics, cpu, memory, disk, remote server, monitoring, stats, statistics, system info, sysinfo, uptime, host metrics, resource usage. No issue asks for host-wide CPU, memory or disk metrics, or a server dashboard. Related, not duplicates:
- #230 (open): database size and free pages inside `state.sqlite`, not volume free space.
- #24, #232 (closed): process-table scan cost. This issue avoids process scans.
- #168 (closed): polling cost while unfocused. This issue streams only while visible.
- #159 (closed): BiBCode's process memory metric on macOS.

items.title: [Package]: SquirrelDisk
items.body:
### Why is it worth to add this package?

**SquirrelDisk** is a free, open-source disk usage analyzer designed to help users identify what is taking up storage space on their computer.

Here are its key features:

* **Compatibility:** It’s a cross-platform tool that works seamlessly on macOS, Windows, and Linux systems.
* **Intuitive Visualization:** It maps your entire disk into colorful graphs in a matter of seconds, allowing you to find large files so you can safely clean them up.
* **Performance:** Built using the Rust programming language, the app is extremely fast and serves as an excellent alternative to well-known software in the same niche, such as WinDirStat, WizTree, TreeSize, and DaisyDisk.
* **Focus on Actual Space:** The program shows the space that files actually occupy on the physical disk, counting files saved only in the cloud (such as on iCloud, Dropbox, Google Drive, and OneDrive) as zero.
* **Remote Analysis:** In addition to local drives, SquirrelDisk can also analyze storage on servers (via SSH) and cloud services.

In short, it’s a lightweight, fast, and highly visual utility for anyone who needs to manage large files and free up space on their hard drive or SSD.

### Home page URL

https://www.squirreldisk.com/

### Source code URL

https://github.com/adileo/squirreldisk

### Packaging policy acknowledgement

- [x] The project is actively developed.
- [x] The project has [existing packages](https://repology.org/projects/) and is "well known".
- [x] Licensed under an [open source license](https://spdx.org/licenses/).
- [x] Not available through a language package manager: cargo, cpan, dotnet tool, gem, npm, pip, etc.

- [x] Not taking up too much disk space (< 100MiB per architecture, exceptions can be made)
- [x] Not duplicating the functionality of existing packages.
- [x] Not serving hacking, malware, phishing, spamming, spying, ddos functionality.
- [x] I certify that I have read [Termux Packaging Policy](https://github.com/termux/termux-packages/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#packaging-policy) and understand that my request will be denied if it is found lacking.

### Additional information

What makes it unique:
- Automatic file cleanup
- Viewing the size of large files with a graphical interface

- This project also includes a CLI that lets you use it from the command line

---
Technically, there is no project in the Termux repository related to this that combines all these benefits into a single project.

milestone.description: Release 0.9.0 to a small circle, then 1.0.0. Order and decisions: the tracking issue "Release 0.9 → 1.0".

items.body:
Decided in the 1.0 grilling (2026-10-03). Distribution is a tagged checkout plus `setup.sh`, for a small circle, on Apple Silicon with macOS 13 or later.

1. **Layout:**
   - The README recommends cloning outside the vault and running `VAULT_ROOT=<vault> ./setup.sh`.
   - Today `VAULT_ROOT` defaults to the repo's parent (`setup.sh:12`), so Obsidian indexes the repo docs, and iCloud syncs the editable install and the `~/bin` targets. `docs/installation.md:216` itself warns against iCloud.
2. **Platform:**
   - setup.sh stops on Intel and on macOS older than 13 with a clear message.
   - The README states the requirements: Apple Silicon, macOS 13 or later, Obsidian 1.11 or later, zsh, disk space and model size.
   - Linux is "not supported".
3. **Uninstall:**
   - `uninstall.sh` removes what setup wrote: the `~/.zprofile` and `~/.zshrc` blocks (marked `# obsidian-ocr-pipeline`), the `~/bin` links, `~/.venvs/{ocrmypdf,mlxocr}`, the model caches and the plugin folder plus its entry in `community-plugins.json`.
   - It lists brew packages without removing them.
4. **Shells:** setup detects `$SHELL` and prints the PATH line for bash or fish instead of silently writing only to `~/.zshrc`.
5. **VENV_ROOT:** a custom `VENV_ROOT` reaches Obsidian started from the Dock (written to a config file the wrappers read) or is documented as unsupported.
6. **Hints:**
   - the `install.sh:53` hint pins `ocrmypdf-appleocr==0.3.4`;
   - the docs state the setup side effects (Homebrew from HEAD, `curl | sh` for uv), and setup asks before installing Homebrew.

## Done when

A fresh macOS user account can install from the README alone, with the checkout outside the vault, and `uninstall.sh` leaves no trace except brew packages. shellcheck passes.

Plugin path: all actions after a fresh install.

items.title: F-10.1a — Remediate production dependency advisories
items.body:
# Proposed F-10.1a — Remediate production dependency advisories

Approved by Philippe on 2026-10-25. Tracked in #135, a focused tranche of #88; do not reopen #27 or close #88. Local verification is complete at 7fc0e81 (runtime patch 7f527fd). Lockfile ownership is released to A. Ready for deliver; Linux CI remains pending after PR publication.

IDs: TECH-01; preserve TECH-07 and SEC-01 guarantees · Choices: D-13 unchanged · Due: final
Depends on: coordination of the shared lockfile with track A, not on corpus functionality.

**Observable goal:** a reproducible production installation and Linux release archive no longer resolve the five identified advisories, while authentication, rooms, races and SSR/no-JavaScript behavior remain unchanged.

## Baseline and ownership

- Scope date: 2026-10-25. `origin/dev`: `2b99993eef9437361e4511ec569a165489a7f3d8`.
- Reserved branch: `fix/f-10-1a-dependency-security`, created from that dev SHA, no upstream push target. Dependency edits and clean installation are complete locally; no push yet.
- Audit was run against the identical dependency manifests/lockfile in the #133 worktree: `npm audit --omit=dev --package-lock-only --json`. Raw evidence: `security-dependencies-audit.json`, next to this card.
- Result: three affected packages, five advisories; one critical and two high package-level findings. Severity does not establish exploitability or compromise.
- Track A's #132 adds `zod: ^4.6.5` to the database workspace and changes the root lockfile. Its range admits the patched version, but its minimum must be coordinated with A. Do not edit A's branch, database manifest, migrations or corpus.
- Track B owns word data, corpus preparation and extension-word implementation. No changes to these files.
- One lockfile writer at a time. Announce the exact baseline and intended package edits before implementation. Preserve A's workspace entries when reconciling; never replace the lockfile wholesale with either side.

## Findings and minimal targets

| Package | Observed | Proposed target | Evidence / exposure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| next | 16.4.0 | 16.4.3, exact | Three advisories below; patch exists and accepts current React 19.3.0 and Node 24. |
| eslint-config-next | 16.4.0 | 16.4.3, exact | Align with Next; not itself an audit finding. |
| zod | 4.6.5 | 4.6.6 in lockfile, direct floor at least 4.6.6 | Oversized collection validation can exhaust memory; preserve all existing payload limits. |
| source-map-js | 1.2.1 | 1.2.2 in lockfile | Present through production Next/PostCSS as well as development tooling; existing ranges admit the patch. |
| sharp | Next currently permits ^0.35.4 | Verify resolved >=0.35.5 | Next 16.4.3 declares ^0.35.5; verify the actual Linux native dependency graph, not just macOS. |

Primary advisory references:

- [GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw): image optimization RCE affecting glibc Linux, patched starting Next 16.4.1; fixed sharp is essential. Azure Linux exposure must be checked against release contents and image configuration.
- [GHSA-p3m5-59mp-jv5r](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p3m5-59mp-jv5r): App Router Server Actions DoS, patched starting 16.4.1. This app uses Server Actions, so the relevant application precondition is present; no attack was performed.
- [GHSA-673q-mjm6-r5xr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-673q-mjm6-r5xr): cache-component typed-array RCE, patched starting 16.4.1. No `use cache` or `cacheComponents` was found in the web source/config examined; do not assert exploitability.
- [GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q): source-map offset processing DoS, fixed in 1.2.2. No attacker-controlled source-map ingestion path has been demonstrated.
- [GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5): Zod collection memory DoS, fixed in 4.6.6. Bounded application inputs reduce exposure but are not substituted for the patch.

**Out of scope:** blanket upgrades, React/Auth.js upgrades, product/UI changes, corpus and bonus implementation, migration changes, security exploits against production, secret changes, cloud actions, merge, deployment. No `npm audit fix --force`, canary upgrade, weakened tests or protections. Additional findings get triaged, not silently added to this card.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Refresh production and full audit baselines on the chosen starting SHA; record each GHSA, versions, applicability and residual findings.
- [ ] Apply only the target package graph changes. Keep Next/eslint-config-next aligned and React/Auth.js unchanged. A owns any database-manifest floor correction until explicitly handed off.
- [ ] Clean `npm ci` succeeds and `npm ls` reports no incompatible or invalid peers. Review the complete lockfile diff, including optional Linux packages. Avoid overrides or new direct dependencies unless normal resolution demonstrably cannot work and the plan is approved again.
- [ ] Final production audit no longer reports the five scoped advisories. Check resolved copies and release archive contents, including sharp >=0.35.5; disclose unrelated or newly published findings separately.
- [ ] Recheck the local Next `notFound()` rule using a disposable old/new-version probe inside and outside the site layout: HTTP status, SSR error body, theme and no-JavaScript rendering. Preserve current behavior unless evidence and approval support changing it.
- [ ] Existing authentication, validation, rooms, races and unknown-route tests pass. Add a focused bounded regression test only where existing tests do not protect an affected path; never use unbounded/OOM payloads or remote exploit probes.
- [ ] Run the required full verification once on the final implementation SHA under the shared heavy-work lock: no-JS guard, lint, types, unit tests, PostgreSQL, drift, production build, E2E and runtime integration. Record skipped PgBouncer checks as unverified, not passed.
- [ ] Verify release packaging on Linux CI and exercise the release artifact through the repository's supported acceptance path. Capture exact SHA/run IDs. Do not claim a macOS build verifies Linux native image dependencies.
- [ ] Code, security, deployment and functional-QA reviews cover the final diff; any subsequent correction receives proportional verification and delta review. Preserve first failures and traces; a green retry is not a diagnosis.
- [ ] Prepare a short human smoke checklist: login, two-account room/course, reload/reconnect, themed unknown URL, no hydration errors. No production action is required to deliver the PR.

**Expected refusals and edge cases:** incompatible peer or runtime → stop and report; unknown lockfile edits → coordinate rather than overwrite; missing Linux/archive evidence → keep that validation pending; unexplained test failure → retain evidence and investigate; new advisory → explicit triage; no disk space → stop before installing/building, do not delete another session's files.

**Data and migrations:** none.

**Likely files:** `apps/web/package.json`, `package-lock.json`; narrowly scoped regression tests if needed; `apps/web/AGENTS.md` only if the observed Next behavior changes; relevant dependency evidence and TECH-01 matrix note. No database manifest without A's handoff, no root CI change by default.

**Evidence:** before/after audit JSON, package metadata and `npm ls`, reviewed lockfile diff, notFound probe report, shared-lock verification log, independent review findings, Linux CI and archive evidence, exact SHAs throughout.

**Reviews:** code-reviewer, security, deployment, functional-qa. DBA not required absent database behavior/schema changes. UI/UX only if an unexpected rendering delta requires an approved UI change.

**Human actions:** Go Ahead for implementation; agree lockfile ownership with A; later explicit delivery approval, human merge, and separate explicit production order. A security fix in dev does not fix production. Do not promote all unfinished dev features merely to deliver this patch; a main-specific hotfix would need separate authorization and scope.

**Risks and unknowns:** approximately 2 GiB disk space was free during scoping, insufficient comfort for an isolated install/build/archive; resolve capacity safely before heavy verification. Installed documentation recommends broader upgrade commands, but this card deliberately uses reviewed patch targets. Current deployed SHA and vulnerability exposure have not been verified remotely. Registry versions and advisories must be rechecked at implementation time.

**Matrix and board:** #135 is in Review after local verification. See the final evidence comment; Linux CI remains pending, and the card is not closed. Keep #88 open for its broader hardening scope. TECH-01 remains partial until the required production validation; do not mark SEC-01/TECH-07 globally complete from a dependency update.

**Delivery boundary:** implementation and verification are authorized. Stop at ready to deliver; push and PR require deliver. No merge or deployment.
