items.title: CI: keep local and CI Xcode versions in step
items.body:
## Problem

Agents build and test with Xcode 27 (Swift 6.4) locally. CI's macOS jobs use the newest stable Xcode on GitHub's `macos-26` image, which is Xcode 26.6 (Swift 6.2). Code that the newer compiler accepts can fail on CI.

That happened on #27: a test closure named a local declared below it. Swift 6.4 resolved the name to the test's own property, and Swift 6.2 rejected it. It cost one CI round, about 15 minutes, and nothing reached `main`. CI caught it, but only after the push, and the next difference could be subtler than a compile error.

The Linux core job uses Swift 6.4, the same as local, so only the Apple-platform jobs are affected.

## Options

1. **Install Xcode 26.6 next to Xcode 27 on the Mac,** and have `make test` build with it when it's there (through `DEVELOPER_DIR`). Local runs then match CI exactly. It costs a large download, which needs the owner's Apple ID, plus disk space.
2. **Wait for GitHub to add Xcode 27 to `macos-26`.** `scripts/select-xcode.sh` already picks the newest stable Xcode, so CI would catch up by itself. Until then, the gap stays.
3. **A check in `make`** that warns when the local Xcode's major version differs from CI's. It's cheap, but it only reminds; it doesn't prevent anything.

**Recommendation:** option 1 for the app and adapter packages until option 2 happens, plus option 3 so the gap is never silent. This matters more near submission (December), when what CI builds must be what ships.

## Done when

- `make test` on the Mac uses the same Xcode major version as CI, or says loudly that it doesn't.
- `CLAUDE.md` says which Xcode builds the release.

items.title: [FEATURE] Visibility and a safe cleanup path for npm cache growth caused by frequent auto-updates (npm global install)
items.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing requests](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20label%3Aenhancement) and this feature hasn't been requested yet
- [x] This is a single feature request (not multiple features)

### Problem Statement

### Summary

With the npm global installation of Claude Code and auto-updates enabled, every new version leaves its package tarballs in the npm cache (`~/.npm/_cacache`). npm documents that its cache grows as new packages are installed and is not pruned automatically, so this is not a bug report against npm's behavior. However, because Claude Code updates very frequently and recent Linux binary packages are about 100–120 MB each, the cache grows steadily on long-running machines. We would like a way to see and safely manage the Claude Code–related portion of that cache.

### Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (x86_64)
- Node.js v22.22.1 (via nvm), npm 10.9.4
- Installation: `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` (currently 2.1.300), auto-updates enabled
- Usage: a server running long-lived sessions

### Measurements (read-only, taken 2026-10-15)

Measured by reading the npm cache index (`~/.npm/_cacache/index-v5`); nothing was deleted, and `npm cache verify` was not run. Sizes are the byte counts recorded in the index; GB here means 10^9 bytes.

- Total size recorded in the npm cache index: 5.94 GB
- Of that, Claude Code–related tarballs: 5.83 GB (about 98%)
- 56 versions are retained, each stored as two entries: the small `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` wrapper package and the platform package `@anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-x64` (about 100–120 MB each in recent versions). 112 entries in total, with no duplicated content.
- Period covered: 2026-08-16 to 2026-10-15 (about 60 days). Averaged over that period, roughly one version per day, i.e. about 100 MB per day.
- Examples of recent entries: 2.1.286 (Oct 1, 108.2 MB), 2.1.293 (Oct 8, 113.1 MB), 2.1.299 (Oct 14, 118.8 MB), 2.1.300 (Oct 15, 119.5 MB).

During the observation period, cached tarballs accumulated across updates; restarting Claude Code sessions did not reclaim that space.

### Proposed Solution

### Request

Any of the following would help:

1. **Visibility**: a way to show how much disk space Claude Code's own packages occupy in the package-manager cache (for example in `claude doctor` or a similar command).
2. **A safe cleanup path**: a command or option that removes cached tarballs of Claude Code versions older than the installed one, **without touching other npm packages' cache entries**.
3. **Or official guidance**: documented, recommended steps for keeping this cache in check on machines that auto-update, so users don't have to resort to clearing the entire npm cache.

### Alternative Solutions

### Related

- #6092 — the same per-version accumulation pattern, but in Bun's global cache (`~/.bun/install/cache`). Closed as not planned (auto-closed after inactivity).
- #11646 — proposal for a `claude clean` command for `~/.claude` caches and logs. It does not cover the npm cache. Closed as not planned (auto-closed after inactivity).

### Priority

Medium - Would be very helpful

### Feature Category

CLI commands and flags

### Use Case Example

_No response_

### Additional Context

_No response_

items.title: [REL-002.12] Bootstrap Installation and Uninstall Lifecycle

milestone.title: M5 — 1.0
milestone.description: The first stable public Horo Engine release meets its supported platform, compatibility, documentation, distribution, migration, and reliability commitments.

items.body:
## Goal

Own first-time installation, operating-system integration, first-launch handoff, repair, and uninstall for users who do not yet have a Horo product installation.

## Scope

- Installation from verified Windows, macOS, and Linux packages into the declared immutable version layout.
- Destination, permission, disk-space, package identity, architecture, minimum-OS, and conflict preflight.
- Desktop, Start menu, application registration, file association, command-line path, and uninstaller integration according to package policy.
- First-launch health result and transition into the normal installed-product/update model.
- Repair and uninstall behavior that preserves projects and explicitly handles settings, caches, logs, credentials, and shared components.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] First installation verifies product identity, signatures, hashes, package layout, platform, and architecture before activation.
- [ ] Failed or interrupted installation cannot leave a falsely active or mixed-version product.
- [ ] First launch produces a bounded health result and a recoverable failure path.
- [ ] Uninstall removes only product-owned installation and registered integration state while preserving user projects and policy-selected user data.
- [ ] Reinstall, repair, already-installed, insufficient-permission, disk-full, locked-file, and shared-component scenarios are covered on supported operating systems.

items.title: feat: publish the Apple Container Linux kernel as a downloadable package
items.body:
## Problem / Background

lablup/backend.ai-go#4294 adds guided provisioning for the Apple Container runtime (epic lablup/backend.ai-go#4130). The runtime's `aigo-container-cli` sidecar needs an arm64 Linux kernel binary to boot guests, and today there is no way for the app to obtain one: users would have to download the ~1 GB kata-containers static tarball and extract a 15 MB file by hand. The app already has a registry download path with progress events, SHA256 verification, and disk-space checks (it reads `packages.json` from this registry), so publishing the extracted kernel here as a package lets the app download 15 MB directly instead of 67x the needed bytes, with no new client-side extraction logic.

## Artifact (source of truth)

Verified working on a macOS 26.6.1 Apple Silicon host on 2026-08-14, using the exact tarball Apple's `container` app pins:

- Upstream archive: kata-containers release `kata-static-3.28.0-arm64.tar.zst`, sha256 `f63d54507d1f18635d94475077e4c2330de4d8e05cedf25f7c38f063b0e66a91`
- Member to extract: `opt/kata/share/kata-containers/vmlinux-6.18.15-186` (uncompressed arm64 vmlinux, ~15 MB)
- Kernel version: 6.18.15-186, from kata-containers release 3.28.0

The package should carry the extracted vmlinux plus metadata recording the upstream kernel version (6.18.15-186), the kata release (3.28.0), the source URL of the upstream tarball, the member path inside it, and the sha256 of both the tarball and the extracted kernel, so provenance is reconstructible from the package alone.

## Licensing (GPLv2 source offer)

The Linux kernel is GPLv2, so redistributing the binary requires a corresponding source offer. The package metadata and this registry's README must include a note pointing at the upstream kata-containers release (tag `3.28.0`) and kernel.org as the corresponding source. No source hosting is needed here as long as the offer points at the canonical upstream. The README's License section, which currently lists per-engine licenses, should gain the kernel entry with this note.

## Package Shape

Follow the registry's existing conventions so the app's engine downloader can fetch it unchanged:

- Package as a `.baiengine`-style tar.gz (or a sibling asset kind if the manifest format does not fit a bare kernel) attached to a GitHub Release, with an entry in `packages.json` under the existing schema (`os`/`arch`/`filename`/`size`/`sha256`)
- Platform key: `darwin` / `arm64` only
- Versioning per the registry's existing scheme: CalVer package version (`YY.M.DD`, like the `26.8.12` engine packages) with the `upstream` field recording the upstream version, mirroring how the mlxcel entry records `26.8.12` alongside `upstream: v0.5.0`. Here `upstream` should identify kata 3.28.0 / vmlinux 6.18.15-186
- Note: the app reads `packages.json`, not `engines.json`, so the new entry must land in `packages.json`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Kernel package built and published as a GitHub Release asset in this registry
- [ ] `packages.json` indexes the package (darwin/arm64, size, sha256, CalVer version, upstream metadata)
- [ ] The download URL returns the kernel and its sha256 matches the documented value
- [ ] Package metadata carries the GPLv2 source-offer note pointing at the upstream kata-containers 3.28.0 release and kernel.org
- [ ] Registry README documents the package, including the source-offer note in the License section
- [ ] lablup/backend.ai-go#4294 can point its downloader at the published package

## References

- App-side counterpart: lablup/backend.ai-go#4294 (guided provisioning for the Apple Container kernel)
- Ancestry: epic lablup/backend.ai-go#4130 (shared container execution backend)

items.title: Deb packages cannot be purged via apt
items.body:
My configuration management system detected that the way your buildkite-agent packages are built for Debian-based systems is not to spec, and prevents the full purging of packages, as per the following demonstration:

```
$ sudo apt install buildkite-agent
Reading package lists... Done
Building dependency tree       
Reading state information... Done
The following NEW packages will be installed:
  buildkite-agent
0 to upgrade, 1 to newly install, 0 to remove and 0 not to upgrade.
Need to get 0 B/12.3 MB of archives.
After this operation, 34.9 MB of additional disk space will be used.
Selecting previously unselected package buildkite-agent.
(Reading database ... 82096 files and directories currently installed.)
Preparing to unpack .../buildkite-agent_3.18.0-3219_amd64.deb ...
Unpacking buildkite-agent (3.18.0-3219) ...
Setting up buildkite-agent (3.18.0-3219) ...
 _           _ _     _ _    _ _                                _
| |         (_) |   | | |  (_) |                              | |
| |__  _   _ _| | __| | | ___| |_ ___    __ _  __ _  ___ _ __ | |_
| '_ \| | | | | |/ _` | |/ / | __/ _ \  / _` |/ _` |/ _ \ '_ \| __|
| |_) | |_| | | | (_| |   <| | ||  __/ | (_| | (_| |  __/ | | | |_
|_.__/ \__,_|_|_|\__,_|_|\_\_|\__\___|  \__,_|\__, |\___|_| |_|\__|
                                               __/ |
                                              |___/

You now need to add your agent token to "/etc/buildkite-agent/buildkite-agent.cfg"
and then you can start your agent by running "sudo systemctl enable buildkite-agent && sudo systemctl start buildkite-agent"
$ sudo apt purge buildkite-agent
Reading package lists... Done
Building dependency tree       
Reading state information... Done
The following packages will be REMOVED:
  buildkite-agent*
0 to upgrade, 0 to newly install, 1 to remove and 0 not to upgrade.
After this operation, 34.9 MB disk space will be freed.
Do you want to continue? [Y/n] 
(Reading database ... 82119 files and directories currently installed.)
Removing buildkite-agent (3.18.0-3219) ...
Stopping buildkite-agent systemd service
Purging configuration files for buildkite-agent (3.18.0-3219) ...
$ ls -la /etc/buildkite-agent/
total 16
drwxr-xr-x   3 buildkite-agent buildkite-agent 4096 Jan 29 17:19 .
drwxr-xr-x 102 root            root            4096 Jan 29 17:19 ..
-rw-------   1 buildkite-agent buildkite-agent 1734 Jan 29 17:19 buildkite-agent.cfg
drwxr-xr-x   2 buildkite-agent buildkite-agent 4096 Jan 29 17:19 hooks
$ dpkg -S /etc/buildkite-agent/buildkite-agent.cfg 
dpkg-query: no path found matching pattern /etc/buildkite-agent/buildkite-agent.cfg
$ 
```
As you can see, `/etc/buildkite-agent` and its contents remain. It didn't take long to find the cause:
```
$ dpkg -e buildkite-agent_3.18.0-3219_amd64.deb 
$ ls -l
total 12064
-rw-r--r-- 1 abolte abolte 12345570 Jan 29 17:26 buildkite-agent_3.18.0-3219_amd64.deb
drwxr-xr-x 2 abolte abolte     4096 Jan 21 16:59 DEBIAN
$ find DEBIAN/
DEBIAN/
DEBIAN/postrm
DEBIAN/prerm
DEBIAN/md5sums
DEBIAN/postinst
DEBIAN/preinst
DEBIAN/control
$ 
```
There is no `conffiles` file, and the `DEBIAN/postinst` script is copying other files that are installed:
https://github.com/buildkite/agent/blob/912a7b544d1ab79e23f1c8e1714fac75b5c561ab/packaging/linux/scripts/after-install-and-upgrade.sh#L36-L37

It goes without saying, that isn't working as intended. `dh_installdeb` is never able to learn about anything deployed under `/etc` on the target system. It's also deploying the same file to a system two times unnecessarily.

For an example of how it should be done, see the lighttpd package shipped with Debian or Ubuntu.
```
$ dpkg -e lighttpd_1.4.35-4ubuntu2.1_amd64.deb
$ dpkg -x lighttpd_1.4.35-4ubuntu2.1_amd64.deb .
$ find etc -type f
etc/lighttpd/lighttpd.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-status.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-cgi.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-evasive.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-rrdtool.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-fastcgi.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-ssl.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-proxy.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/05-auth.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-dir-listing.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-usertrack.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-ssi.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/15-fastcgi-php.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/11-extforward.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-no-www.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-accesslog.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/README
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/90-debian-doc.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-userdir.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-flv-streaming.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-expire.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-simple-vhost.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-evhost.conf
etc/cron.daily/lighttpd
etc/ufw/applications.d/lighttpd
etc/logrotate.d/lighttpd
etc/init.d/lighttpd
$ cat DEBIAN/conffiles 
/etc/cron.daily/lighttpd
/etc/init.d/lighttpd
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/05-auth.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-accesslog.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-cgi.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-dir-listing.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-evasive.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-evhost.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-expire.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-fastcgi.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-flv-streaming.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-no-www.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-proxy.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-rrdtool.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-simple-vhost.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-ssi.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-ssl.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-status.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-userdir.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-usertrack.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/11-extforward.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/15-fastcgi-php.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/90-debian-doc.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/README
/etc/lighttpd/lighttpd.conf
/etc/logrotate.d/lighttpd
/etc/ufw/applications.d/lighttpd
$ # Yes they're the same:
$ diff <(find etc -type f | sort) <(sort DEBIAN/conffiles | cut -d '/' -f 2-)
```

The `conffiles` is just there in the above example for backwards compatibility with older systems, since newer systems will know that files under `/etc` are config files automatically - but it's probably a good idea for you to follow suit given the older distribution releases supported.

I think you should include your configuration files along with all the other files (removing lines in the shell scripts to copy them), and then specify those in `conffiles`. At this point apt should start behaving correctly (for config files at least). See https://www.debian.org/doc/manuals/maint-guide/dother.en.html for details.

I note in https://github.com/buildkite/agent/blob/master/scripts/build-debian-package.sh you're using the `fpm` tool to generate packages. I'm personally not a fan of packaging without standard Debian tools (surely the linter would have flagged such issues?) but a quick search suggests there is a `--config-files` argument available which may help.

https://github.com/jordansissel/fpm/pull/506/files

One thing that should be in the `postrm` script that isn't, are commands like:
```
deluser buildkite-agent || true
delgroup buildkite-agent || true
```
As it stands, the `buildkite-agent` user and group is also still left around on the system after purging.

If using fpm, you might consider employing the use of a free software tool like [AIDE](https://aide.github.io/) to ensure the package install/upgrade/remove/purge functions are behaving correctly.

items.title: Proposal: support bun install for faster, smaller installs (no runtime change)
items.body:
A lot of the work on Kong Royale now runs through coding agents, which clone and install the repo many times, often several checkouts side by side on one machine. I measured whether Bun's package manager helps with that, and whether Bun as a runtime is worth it. In short, the package manager helps, mostly with disk space, and needs nothing from you. The runtime doesn't, because it changes the simulation's results.

**Measurements.** All on one machine: Linux x86_64, 4 vCPU, Node 22.23.4, npm 10.9.9, Bun 1.4.4. Runs were interleaved, and each tool had its own empty cache for the cold runs.

| | `npm ci` | `bun install --frozen-lockfile` |
|---|---|---|
| Install, cold cache (5 runs, median) | 1.94 s | 0.26 s |
| Install, warm cache (5 runs, median) | 1.61 s | 0.05 s |
| `node_modules` | 140 MB | 130 MB |
| Disk for one checkout, cache included | 180 MB | 130 MB |
| 8 checkouts installed in parallel: wall time | 6.0 s | 0.12 s |
| 8 checkouts installed in parallel: extra disk | 1.21 GB | 7.5 MB |
| `npm run build` / `npm test` | pass / 11 of 11 | pass / 11 of 11 |
| `dist/` | | byte-identical to the npm install |

Bun reads `package-lock.json` directly and installs the same versions. The one exception is sharp's unused WebAssembly fallback, which it skips. It writes no `bun.lock`, and it refuses to run if `package.json` and the lockfile disagree.

The disk saving comes from hardlinking out of Bun's global cache (on macOS, `clonefile`). That only helps checkouts on the same disk, not separate machines. The time saved is under 2 s per install, so disk is the real gain.

**Runtime: not proposed.** Under Bun, most things work and are faster: server boot, `ws`, `netlab --check`, the build, and 11 of 11 tests. But the simulation produces a different match. `sim-smoke trios 42` gives state hash `d802631a` under Bun, against `c8f3110c` under Node. The cause is that JavaScriptCore's `Math.sin`, `cos`, `atan2`, `exp`, `pow` and others return different last bits from V8's, and `shared/sim` uses them. Each runtime is deterministic on its own, but a Bun server would not reproduce Node's matches. So the runtime stays Node.

**Proposal**
1. **Docs only (the PR linked below).** Document `bun install --frozen-lockfile` as an optional alternative to `npm ci`. npm stays the source of truth for dependencies, and everything runs on Node. Nothing changes in `package.json`, the lockfile or CI.
2. **Optional follow-up, if you want it guarded.** A small CI job that runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` (with `oven-sh/setup-bun` pinned to a commit), then the existing build and test on Node. It would catch a lockfile that Bun can't read. Happy to send it if you'd like.

**Not proposed:** replacing `package-lock.json` with `bun.lock`. That would make Bun required for everyone.

**Risks**
- Bun only runs install scripts for trusted packages. esbuild and sharp work as they are, and build and test pass.
- On Linux and Windows, hand-editing a file in `node_modules` also edits the cached copy shared with other checkouts.
- So far I've verified this on Linux only.

If you'd rather keep the project npm-only, that's fine too. Contributors can still use Bun locally without any change on your side.

items.title: Build an AppImage for Linux
items.body:
There have been a ton of weird bugs when running ntsc-rs on Debian (https://github.com/valadaptive/ntsc-rs/issues/224, https://github.com/valadaptive/ntsc-rs/issues/307, https://github.com/valadaptive/ntsc-rs/issues/310), caused by Debian's policy of shipping ancient versions of packages combined with GStreamer's reliance on varied and intricate multimedia libraries.

I'm not sure how difficult it is to build an AppImage, but it would solve a lot of the weird library versioning issues at the expense of download size and disk space. Compared to Flatpak and Snap, it has the advantage of not requiring any external runtime or package manager.

items.title: PigTree v1.0 Product Specification: Local Disk Space Analyzer & Guarded Remediation

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent

items.body:
## Problem Statement

Everyday Windows users frequently encounter low-disk-space warnings and acute storage crises. When attempting to reclaim space, they face overwhelming friction, confusion, and anxiety:
1. **Misleading Disk Accounting & Duplicate Inflation**: Existing Windows disk analyzers (such as WizTree, TreeSize, WinDirStat, and SpaceSniffer) present conflicting or deceptive numbers. They routinely double-count NTFS Hard Links across directories (such as `C:\Windows\System32` and `C:\Windows\WinSxS`), confusing users into believing system components consume twice their actual space. They frequently conflate Logical Size (file addressable byte length) with Allocated Size (on-disk physical cluster allocation), erroneously reporting 0-byte online-only cloud placeholders (such as OneDrive or Dropbox files) as multi-gigabyte disk hogs.
2. **Inaccessible Space & Missing Reconciliation**: When permissions prevent standard user accounts from inspecting protected directories (such as `System Volume Information` or other user profiles), existing tools either silently omit the storage or report it as 0 bytes, creating huge, unexplained discrepancies between reported directory totals and actual drive capacity. Users are left wondering where 30–100 GB of drive space has vanished.
3. **High Anxiety & Cryptic System Structures**: Ordinary users cannot distinguish between safe user caches and fragile operating system dependencies. Faced with cryptic folders like `WinSxS`, `DriverStore`, `ProgramData\Package Cache`, and `AppData\Local\Temp`, users fear rendering Windows unbootable or losing critical personal files.
4. **Unguarded, Destructive Cleanup**: Traditional utilities offer blunt, unvalidated deletion mechanisms (such as unguided "Shift+Delete" or crude folder-level wipes). They fail to perform live preflight checks before modifying the filesystem, lack awareness of file modifications occurring between scan and deletion, offer no rollback safeguards, miscalculate reclaimable space when deleting hard-linked files, and fail to provide native OS handoffs for system-managed storage.
5. **Privilege Overreach & Security Hazards**: Most high-speed analyzers demand full Administrator elevation upon launch or install persistent elevated background services, expanding the system attack surface and preventing standard-user execution on managed or family PCs.
6. **Accessibility & Visualization Disparity**: Dense visual representations like treemaps are universally treated as graphical-only canvas widgets devoid of keyboard navigation, screen-reader semantics, and high-contrast support, effectively locking out users who rely on assistive technologies.
7. **Brittle Automation & Closed Ecosystems**: Power users, IT professionals, and automation workflows lack a unified, transport-neutral tool that provides identical information fidelity, machine-readable structured streams (NDJSON, JSON, CSV), and versioned, reopenable historical snapshot files across both a modern graphical desktop interface and a headless command-line interface.

## Solution

PigTree v1.0 is an open-source, local-first Windows disk space analyzer and guarded remediation application designed for Windows 10 and 11 (x64). It bridges the gap between everyday simplicity and expert-grade precision through absolute domain correctness, truth-in-accounting, progressive disclosure, and guarded, reversible remediation.

Key solution pillars include:
- **Canonical Information Model & Truth-in-Accounting**: Clear architectural separation between Directory Entries (names/paths) and Filesystem Objects (underlying storage entities). Comprehensive tracking of Hard Link aliases, Content Streams (alternate data streams), and Storage Characteristics (sparse, filesystem-compressed, online-only). Whole-volume Capacity reconciliation explicitly balances `Capacity = Free Space + Used Space`, attributing Used Space into `Accounted Unique Allocation` and a clearly reported `Reconciliation Difference` (surfaced as `Unattributed Used Space` or `Over-Accounted Allocation`), eliminating mysterious missing space.
- **Local Filesystem Matrix & Least-Privilege Execution**: Comprehensive local filesystem support covering NTFS, ReFS, FAT32, and exFAT across whole local Volumes and arbitrary local directory folders on fixed and removable storage. Seven distinct executables with strictly separated roles enforce standard-user execution by default via documented Win32 traversal across all supported filesystems in a disposable worker process. An optional, short-lived, user-authorized elevated broker acquiring read-only volume handles for an isolated, sandboxed raw MFT parser provides NTFS-only whole-volume acceleration protected by fail-closed invariant validation gates and seamless fallback to elevated Win32 traversal. Zero persistent elevated background daemons.
- **Synchronized, Accessible Dual Workspaces**: Question-first **Overview Cards** ("What is taking up space?", "Large archives & installers", "Forgotten media & old files", "Duplicate candidates") guide casual users directly to safe reclamation opportunities. These link directly into a unified **Explorer Workspace** combining a virtualized Tree-Table, a Direct3D 11 GPU-accelerated Treemap hosted via `D3DImage`, Flat File views, Top-N Largest Files, Extension/Type distributions, and Age breakdowns. The graphical treemap and virtualized tree-grid maintain truthful, bounded UI Automation (UIA) accessibility with full keyboard navigation, Windows High Contrast theme tracking, and 200% text scaling.
- **Guarded Remediation & Content-Verified Deduplication**: A 5-stage guided duplicate review workflow (Candidates → Verification → Keeper Selection → Action Configuration → Action Plan) powered by progressive BLAKE3/SHA-256 stream hashing, hard-link alias awareness, and cloud hydration consent gates. All filesystem modifications are governed by immutable **Action Plans** partitioned by additive Action Risk Classes (`routine`, `caution`, `protected`, `prohibited`) and validated by a **Live Preflight** check (verifying file IDs, stream counts, timestamps, sizes, and attributes immediately prior to per-step Commit Points). Deletions default to the Windows Recycle Bin (`IFileOperation`); same-volume NTFS Hard Link consolidation operates via a journaled recovery mechanism with a local Recovery Vault or immediate-reclaim staging; and protected system paths are routed safely to native Windows settings and maintenance applets.
- **Transport-Neutral Shared Engine**: A core Rust engine (`pigtree-engine.exe`) encapsulates all scanning orchestration, query evaluation, duplicate candidate grouping, snapshot persistence, and mutation planning. Both the WPF GUI client (`PigTree.exe`) and the headless CLI client (`pigtree.exe`) interact with the engine via Protocol Buffers (protobuf v3) over bounded, framed duplex byte-mode Named Pipes.
- **Immutable Snapshot Files & Reopenability**: Analyses can be saved to and reopened from immutable `.pts` (base snapshot) and `.ptse` (snapshot enrichment) files utilizing 64-bit aligned memory-mapped columnar tables, Compressed Sparse Row (CSR) graph indexing, chunk-level LZ4 compression where specified, and layered CRC-32/BLAKE3 integrity verification, allowing historical review without rescanning.
- **Strict Privacy & Zero Off-Device Telemetry**: All filenames, paths, hashes, and metadata remain strictly local to the user's device. Diagnostic exports provide deterministic, versioned redaction capabilities (`obfuscate_paths`, `mask_user_identities`, `scrub_native_messages`), with redacted output carrying zero mutation authority.

## User Stories

### Everyday and Expert Analysis
1. As an everyday user, I want plain-language overview cards answering "What is eating my space?", so that I can immediately understand the largest contributors to disk usage without navigating complex folder trees.
2. As an everyday user, I want clear guidance on whether large folders (such as Downloads or Temp caches) can be safely reviewed for cleanup, so that I can free disk space without fear of damaging my operating system.
3. As an everyday user, I want system-critical folders (like WinSxS, DriverStore, and System Volume Information) clearly labeled with explanations and safe native cleanup recommendations, so that I do not attempt dangerous manual deletions.
4. As an everyday user, I want to view my disk usage broken down by intuitive categories (such as Games, Media, Documents, and System), so that I can locate forgotten personal files quickly.
5. As an expert user, I want a high-density, multi-column tree-table displaying Referenced Allocated Size, Unique Allocated Size, Logical Size, Hard Link reference counts, and Object IDs, so that I can perform rigorous storage audits.
6. As an expert user, I want to inspect individual named Content Streams (Alternate Data Streams) on any filesystem object, so that I can identify hidden stream storage like Zone.Identifier or custom application metadata.
7. As an expert user, I want to inspect Reparse Point tags and targets without traversal loops, so that I can understand directory junctions, symlinks, and volume mount points.
8. As an expert user, I want to inspect security attributes (Owner SID and Access Control Rules) for scanned items, so that I can diagnose permission-related space anomalies.
9. As an expert user, I want to toggle between Referenced Allocated Size and Unique Allocated Size across tree views, so that I can see the exact difference between folder tree references and distinct physical data allocations.

### Target Selection
10. As a user, I want to select any mounted local drive letter as a Scan Target across supported filesystems (NTFS, ReFS, FAT32, and exFAT), so that I can analyze fixed internal SSDs, HDDs, and removable USB drives.
11. As a user, I want to select a mounted volume that lacks an assigned drive letter as a Scan Target, so that I can inspect recovery partitions or unlettered system volumes.
12. As a user, I want to select a single local directory folder on fixed or removable storage across any supported filesystem (NTFS, ReFS, FAT32, or exFAT) as a Scan Target, so that I can analyze a specific project or user profile without scanning the entire drive.
13. As a user, I want the application to validate the availability and readiness of a selected Scan Target before starting, so that I receive immediate, actionable error messages if a removable drive is disconnected or formatted with an unsupported filesystem.

### Profiles, Runs, Snapshots, Coverage, Knowledge, and Accounting
14. As a user, I want to choose an Analysis Profile (such as Fast Default, Comprehensive Streams, or Custom) before running a scan, so that I can balance scan speed against metadata depth.
15. As a user, I want each scan execution to be tracked as a discrete, time-bounded Analysis Run with recorded start and completion timestamps, so that I know exactly when the observations were made.
16. As a user, I want the scan output to be preserved as an immutable Analysis Snapshot, so that subsequent filtering, viewing, and historical comparisons operate on a stable, tamper-proof dataset.
17. As a user, I want to see the overall Scope Coverage state (Complete, Partial, or Indeterminate) for my scan, so that I know whether the data represents the entire target or contains unobserved areas.
18. As a user, I want every unobserved area recorded as a distinct Coverage Gap with its specific failure reason (such as Access Denied, Path Too Long, or Device I/O Error), so that I can understand why certain folders could not be analyzed.
19. As a user, I want every displayed metadata value to carry an explicit Value Knowledge status (Known, Not Observed, Unavailable, or Not Applicable), so that missing values are never misrepresented as zero.
20. As a user analyzing a whole Volume, I want a complete Capacity reconciliation that balances Capacity into Free Space, Used Space, Accounted Unique Allocation, and Reconciliation Difference (surfaced as Unattributed Used Space or Over-Accounted Allocation), so that I never experience unexplained missing disk space.
21. As a user analyzing a whole Volume, I want Unattributed Used Space clearly explained (e.g. filesystem metadata, shadow copies, or unreadable system space) and segregated from normal directories, so that I am not misled into believing it is a deletable folder.
22. As a user analyzing a whole Volume where allocations exceed reported usage due to snapshot timing differences, I want Over-Accounted Allocation clearly flagged as a timing discrepancy rather than an error, so that I understand filesystem churn effects.
23. As a user analyzing a directory Scan Target, I want external hard links clearly marked with External Reference Uncertainty, so that I understand why deleting a directory entry may not free physical disk allocation.
24. As a user, I want to save an immutable Analysis Snapshot to disk as a `.pts` file and reopen it later, so that I can review historical scans without re-scanning the storage device.
25. As a user, I want to attach on-demand Snapshot Enrichments (`.ptse` files) containing hash or owner metadata to an existing snapshot without mutating the original base snapshot, so that I can build upon previous scans cleanly.

### Visualization and Accessibility Parity

## Implementation Decisions

### 1. Multi-Process Topology and Process Isolation
To satisfy strict security, privilege separation, memory safety, and UI responsiveness requirements, PigTree v1.0 adopts a multi-process architecture consisting of seven distinct executables:
- **Presentation Client (`PigTree.exe` / `pigtree.exe`)**:
  - The desktop GUI (`PigTree.exe`) is built on C# and the latest supported .NET LTS using Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF), running as a standard non-elevated user process. Responsible for visual layout, user interaction, bounded accessibility providers, and clipboard/shell handoffs. Contains zero filesystem scanning, raw parsing, or mutation logic.
  - The CLI (`pigtree.exe`) is a lightweight, non-elevated native binary written in Rust. Responsible for parsing CLI flags, dispatching commands to the session host, and formatting streaming outputs (NDJSON, JSON, CSV).
- **Private Session Host Engine (`pigtree-engine.exe`)**:
  - A headless core engine and private session host written in Rust, running at standard medium integrity.
  - Implements the transport-neutral domain contract, in-memory graph indexing, columnar snapshot store, typed query algebra, preflight validation, and worker lifecycle orchestration.
  - Dedicated 1:1 per client process (GUI or CLI); persistent multi-tenant background daemons are prohibited.
  - Bound strictly to the client's lifecycle via Windows Job Objects configured with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`, preventing orphaned background processes.
- **Disposable Scan Worker (`pigtree-scan-worker.exe`)**:
  - A short-lived, disposable Rust worker spawned by the Session Host to execute non-elevated Win32 directory traversal across all supported filesystems.
  - Operates under standard user tokens with restricted rights; terminates immediately upon scan completion or cancellation.
- **Elevated Scan Broker (`pigtree-elevated-broker.exe`)**:
  - A short-lived elevated helper built in Rust, launched on-demand via UAC elevation (`ShellExecuteExW` with `runas`) solely when raw volume scanning or backup privilege is authorized by the user.
  - Acquires `SeBackupPrivilege` and raw volume handles (`\\.\<Volume>`). Contains zero uncontracted raw parsing logic.
- **Sandboxed Raw MFT Parser (`pigtree-raw-parser.exe`)**:
  - An untrusted parser process built in Rust, spawned by the elevated broker under a restricted security token (stripping administrative SIDs and privileges) or AppContainer isolation.
  - Consumes raw MFT streams across an inherited read-only handle, validates structural invariants, and emits parsed metadata records over an anonymous pipe to the broker.
- **Mutation Worker (`pigtree-mutation-worker.exe`)**:
  - A dedicated, short-lived mutation execution helper built in Rust, spawned on demand per authorized execution group (at medium or elevated integrity as required by the Action Plan).
  - Authenticates using a single-use plan nonce and cryptographic digest of the exact, immutable Action Plan. Validates live preconditions, executes guarded commit points, generates execution records, and terminates immediately.

### 2. Inter-Process Communication (IPC) Transport, Framing, and Identity
All inter-process communication adheres to strictly defined transport, framing, serialization, and authentication boundaries:
- **Client to Private Session Host (`PigTree.exe` / `pigtree.exe` <-> `pigtree-engine.exe`)**:
  - *Transport*: Bounded, framed duplex byte-mode local Named Pipes (`\\.\pipe\pigtree-engine-{session_id}`). Message-mode pipes, shared writable ring buffers, and transport compression are explicitly prohibited.
  - *Serialization*: Protocol Buffers (protobuf v3) for strongly typed cross-language RPC commands, query requests, challenge dialogues, and coalescible progress notifications.
  - *Identity & Security*: Client launches the engine passing a session identifier and pipe endpoint via non-secret command-line arguments. Same-integrity bootstrap credentials are delivered via an inherited read-only handle. Mutual live process identity verification is enforced upon connection (`GetNamedPipeServerProcessId` and `GetNamedPipeClientProcessId`). An ephemeral channel key is established over the pipe before commands are accepted. Zero secrets are passed via command-line arguments.
- **Session Host to Disposable Scan Worker (`pigtree-engine.exe` <-> `pigtree-scan-worker.exe`)**:
  - Dedicated inherited anonymous data pipe carrying versioned packed Little-Endian binary observation records from worker to engine.
  - Cancellation is handled via a dedicated inherited Win32 manual-reset cancellation event handle (`CreateEventW`) checked concurrently during I/O, with structured diagnostics directed to an inherited stderr pipe.
- **Session Host to Elevated Broker & Raw Parser**:
  - The elevated broker connects back to the engine's elevated-restricted Named Pipe. The engine verifies high integrity and elevated token privileges via `GetNamedPipeClientProcessId` and `OpenProcessToken` before establishing the channel key.
  - The broker opens the read-only volume handle, creates a restricted token/AppContainer, and spawns `pigtree-raw-parser.exe` with the inherited read-only handle and an inherited anonymous pipe.
  - The parser streams versioned packed Little-Endian metadata records over the anonymous pipe to the broker for invariant validation before forwarding to the engine.
- **Session Host to Mutation Worker (`pigtree-engine.exe` <-> `pigtree-mutation-worker.exe`)**:
  - Dedicated byte-mode bounded framed Named Pipe using Protobuf v3 for mutation control, authenticated via single-use plan nonce and cryptographic digest.
- **CLI Standard Stream Contracts**:
  - `stdout`: Newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) for event streams, JSON for synchronous queries, and RFC 4180 CSV for tabular output.
  - `stderr`: Structured diagnostic messages, human-readable status logs, and error traces.

### 3. Deep Observation Seam, Scan Planner, and Raw MFT Release Gate
- The scanning subsystem interacts with the rest of the application strictly across a transport-neutral deep observation seam.
- **Supported Local Filesystem Matrix**: PigTree v1.0 supports NTFS, ReFS, FAT32, and exFAT across whole local Volumes (with or without assigned drive letters) and arbitrary local directory folders on fixed internal disks and removable storage devices.
- **Inputs**: Exactly one Scan Target (Volume or Directory), an Analysis Profile, a Security/Privilege Policy, a Resource Budget, a Progress Sink, and a Cooperative Cancellation Token.
- **Outputs**: A streaming sequence of Observation Envelopes, structured Coverage Gaps, provenance metadata, adapter lifecycle events, and a terminal Run Outcome.
- **Scan Adapter Hierarchy & Fallback Matrix**:
  - *Win32 Traversal Adapter*: Universal traversal engine covering all supported filesystems (NTFS, ReFS, FAT32, exFAT), arbitrary directory Scan Targets, non-elevated executions, and elevated fallback cases via standard recursive enumeration (`FindFirstFileExW` / `FindNextFileW` using `FindExInfoBasic` and `FIND_FIRST_EX_LARGE_FETCH`, with documented `GetFileInformationByHandleEx` directory batching where applicable).
  - *Raw MFT Adapter*: Dedicated, NTFS-only whole-volume acceleration parsing NTFS `$MFT` records. Raw MFT parsing is not applicable to ReFS, FAT32, or exFAT volumes.
- **Stable-Release Verification Gate for Raw MFT**:
  - The raw MFT adapter is **disabled by default in stable production releases** until five mandatory release gates pass:
    1. Differential scanning tests comparing raw output against documented Win32 traversal across standard and synthetic corpora;
    2. Malformed and corrupted MFT fuzzing to verify parser isolation and crash resilience;
    3. Windows and NTFS version compatibility matrices (covering cluster sizes, record sizes, and feature flags);
    4. Interruption and cancellation stress tests under active filesystem churn;
    5. Demonstrable end-to-end benchmark performance advantages over optimized Win32 traversal on representative hardware.
  - Until all gates pass, elevated NTFS scans default safely to documented elevated Win32 traversal.
  - When enabled, runtime invariant checks, whole-volume capacity reconciliation, and bounded deterministic API sampling are enforced, triggering immediate visible fallback to Win32 traversal upon disagreement.

### 4. Canonical Information Model and Storage Accounting Engine
- **Entries vs. Objects**: Distinct representation of Directory Entries (paths, names, parent links) and Filesystem Objects (underlying storage entities identified by Volume GUID + File ID / Object ID).
- **Hard Link Tracking**: Multiple Directory Entries referencing the same Filesystem Object are recorded as aliases. Unique Allocated Size attributes physical storage exactly once per distinct object.
- **Content Streams**: Full support for primary unnamed data streams and named secondary streams (Alternate Data Streams), tracking individual stream logical sizes, allocated sizes, and storage characteristics.
- **Storage Characteristics**: Explicit tracking of sparse files, filesystem-compressed streams, deduplicated clusters, and cloud-reparse placeholders (`FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT`, `IO_REPARSE_TAG_CLOUD`, `IO_REPARSE_TAG_ONEDRIVE`). Online-only placeholders report 0 bytes physical disk allocation regardless of logical size.
- **Four-State Value Knowledge**: Every metadata property is tracked as `Known`, `Not Observed`, `Unavailable` (with explicit reason), or `Not Applicable`.
- **Scope Coverage**: Evaluated relative to the Analysis Profile as `Complete`, `Partial`, or `Indeterminate`. Coverage Gaps record path bounds, observation status, and failure error codes.
- **Whole-Volume Capacity Reconciliation**:
  - Strictly enforces `Volume Capacity = Free Space + Used Space`.
  - Reconciles `Used Space = Accounted Unique Allocation + Reconciliation Difference`.
  - Positive discrepancy is surfaced as `Unattributed Used Space` (system metadata, shadow copies, unreadable directories).
  - Negative discrepancy is surfaced as `Over-Accounted Allocation` (filesystem churn during scan).
  - Both states are clearly separated from normal directory nodes in all views.
- **Directory Target Accounting**: Directory scans report reachable Referenced and Unique aggregates and explicitly mark external hard-link boundaries with `External Reference Uncertainty`, omitting whole-volume capacity reconciliation.

### 5. Immutable Snapshot Persistence Format (`.pts` / `.ptse`)
- **Binary Architecture**: Immutable, versioned, Little-Endian, 64-bit aligned memory-mapped columnar layout.
- **Base Snapshot (`.pts`)**:
  - Header: Magic bytes, format version, volume identity, scan target, analysis profile, observation interval timestamps, run outcome, and root coverage state.
  - Columnar Storage: Core attributes (sizes, identities, reference counts, topology offsets) are stored as independent, contiguous primitive columnar arrays, enabling demand-paged OS virtual memory utilization and zero-copy slice casting via `zerocopy` / `bytemuck` without full-file heap deserialization.
  - Graph Hierarchy: Compressed Sparse Row (CSR) index for $O(1)$ child lookups and linear memory traversals during subtree aggregations.
  - Compression: Chunk-level LZ4 compression where specified for cold storage.
  - Layered Integrity: Chunk-level CRC-32 checksums paired with snapshot-level BLAKE3 verification covering all payload sections.
- **Snapshot Enrichment (`.ptse`)**:
  - Append-only auxiliary format referencing a base `.pts` by base snapshot hash and volume identity.
  - Stores on-demand metadata: full/partial content hashes, Owner SIDs, ACL descriptors, and verification scopes.
  - Loading an enrichment creates an immutable composite view without mutating the base `.pts` file.
- **Atomic Settlement**: Base snapshots and enrichments are written to temporary staging files, verified for internal consistency and checksum integrity, and atomically committed via file rename.

### 6. Presentation, Virtualization, and Accessibility Architecture
- **Framework**: WPF on C# / latest supported .NET LTS using modern Fluent styling, running in 64-bit user mode.
- **Tree-Table Virtualization**:
  - Implemented via a customized `ListView` paired with a recycling `VirtualizingStackPanel` (`VirtualizationMode="Recycling"`, `ScrollUnit="Pixel"`).
  - Backed by a `VirtualTreeCollection` implementing a flattened virtual projection model with a bounded sliding-window page cache (200–500 active rows). WPF never constructs a full managed object mirror for 5,000,000 entries.
  - Synchronous index lookups return lightweight placeholder items during rapid scrolling while fetching row data asynchronously from the engine over IPC.
- **Hardware-Accelerated Treemap Visualization**:
  - Rendered using Direct3D 11 hosted inside WPF exclusively via `System.Windows.Interop.D3DImage` using a legacy DXGI shared handle to a Direct3D 9Ex surface. `HwndHost` is explicitly not used.
  - **In-Process Presentation Geometry**: The Rust engine supplies semantic node weights and hierarchy; the WPF presentation layer calculates squarified $(x, y, w, h)$ bounding geometry locally in C# against active viewport pixel dimensions.
  - Cushion shading and boundaries are rendered in hardware via HLSL pixel shaders.
  - Conservative synchronization: `ID3D11DeviceContext::Flush()` followed by `D3DImage.AddDirtyRect` on the UI thread, with robust recovery handling for device loss, `IsFrontBufferAvailableChanged`, and software fallbacks.
- **Truthful Bounded UI Automation (UIA) and Accessibility**:
  - Custom automation peers expose a truthful, bounded UIA tree covering realized items only.
  - `FindItemByProperty` evaluates cached items only, returning null for uncached items rather than blocking the UI thread or attempting to realize the entire tree into managed memory. Full search is delegated through engine-backed filtered projection queries.
  - Item realization (`Realize`) succeeds for cached providers and cleanly surfaces when items are evicted (`ElementNotAvailable` / `UIA_E_ELEMENTNOTAVAILABLE`).
  - Windows High Contrast (Forced Colors) themes integrate dynamically with system theme brush keys across tree-table controls and treemap borders.
  - Full Per-Monitor DPI V2 awareness and text scaling up to 200%.

### 7. Guided Duplicate Remediation Engine & Verification Subsystem
- **5-Stage State Pipeline**:
  ```
  [1. Candidate Sets] -> [2. Progressive Verification] -> [3. Keeper Selection] -> [4. Action Configuration] -> [5. Action Plan Formulation]
  ```
- **Candidate Discovery**: Groups distinct Filesystem Objects sharing identical Logical Size and matching Preliminary Classification rules. Rejects path aliases sharing the same File ID.
- **Verification Subsystem**:
  - *Verification Scope*: Defaults strictly to the unnamed data stream. Named alternate streams are verified only when explicitly requested.
  - *Progressive Verification Pipeline*:
    1. Header Hash (first 64 KB via BLAKE3).
    2. Sparse Chunk Sample (header, midpoint, tail).
    3. Full Stream Hash (sequential BLAKE3 / SHA-256).
    4. Optional Byte-by-Byte comparison for complete certainty.
  - *Cloud Hydration Safety*: Scans detect `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT` and cloud storage tags. Any candidate requiring online hydration triggers a mandatory, non-dismissible Cloud Hydration Consent challenge. If declined, the item remains unverified and locked from automated actions.
- **Keeper Selection**: Rule-based keeper suggestions (such as "Keep newest", "Keep oldest", "Keep shortest path", "Keep most accessible") or manual user selection, ensuring exactly one primary copy is preserved per duplicate set.

### 8. Guarded Mutation Engine, Live Preflight, and Recovery Subsystem
- **Additive Action Risk Classes**:
  - `routine`: Standard safeguards and single preview confirmation suffice. Indicates ordinary operational parameters; not a claim that deletion is universally safe.
  - `caution`: Elevated uncertainty or operational risk (such as External Reference Uncertainty, non-empty structures, or elevated privilege); requires focused reason acknowledgement.
  - `protected`: Targets managed by Windows or cloud providers (component stores, driver stores, page/swap/hibernation files, shadow copies, package stores, installed applications, or cloud-managed entries); direct mutation is replaced with structured native/provider handoff.
  - `prohibited`: No sufficiently safe or authorized mutation path exists (e.g. active PigTree recovery vaults, execution journals, active records, unknown Reparse Point tags, unmatched duplicate streams, or EFS deduplication in v1). Direct mutation is completely blocked.
- **Safeguard Catalog**: A versioned local catalog of protection rules ships with releases. Custom rules can be added, but built-in rules cannot be disabled or weakened.
- **Live Preflight Validation Engine**:
  - Executes immediately prior to per-step Commit Points. Re-observes target entries and verifies:
    1. Target File ID matches expected Object ID.
    2. Content Stream count and stream sizes match snapshot.
    3. Last Write Timestamp matches snapshot within acceptable tolerance.
    4. File attributes match (rejecting unexpected read-only, hidden, or system flags).
    5. Parent directory identity remains valid and unchanged.
    6. Reparse point target integrity is preserved.
    7. Sufficient destination volume free space exists for recovery staging.
  - *Staleness & Invalidation*: Any preflight mismatch immediately marks the operation as `Stale/Prohibited`, aborts execution for that target, and requires a fresh scan. In-place overrides of failed preflights are strictly prohibited.
- **Remediation Execution Mechanics**:
  - *Recycle Bin Deletion*: Executed via Windows Shell COM `IFileOperation` with `FOF_ALLOWUNDO`. Preflight evaluates volume support, quota, and thresholds. Immediate Reclaimable Allocation is reported as zero (conditional upon eventual purge).
  - *Permanent Deletion*: Standard per-entry Win32 primitives without privilege-bypassing flags (prohibiting POSIX force unlinking, automatic read-only clearing, delayed reboot deletion, or permission bypasses).
  - *Same-Volume NTFS Hard Link Replacement*:
    - Requires stable File Reference Numbers, verified link counts, complete relevant Coverage, matching Owner/ACLs, and full verification of all content-bearing streams. Prohibited for Reparse Points, cloud files, package stores (`WindowsApps`), and EFS-encrypted files.
    - *Recoverable Mode*: Creates a preservation Hard Link to the victim object in a deterministic restricted per-volume PigTree recovery vault (location-neutral). Immediate reclaim is 0 bytes (storage retained in vault until dedicated purge plan).
    - *Immediate-Reclaim Mode*: Creates a temporary staging link in a plan-owned staging area, executes rename-over commit point, purges staging link. Irreversible immediate allocation release.
    - *Journaled Commit Points*: Per-step local journal with same-volume rename-over. Failure before or at the Commit Point halts the group and restores the in-flight entry. No false global filesystem transactionality is assumed.
- **Execution Records (`.pter` Files)**: Immutable JSON/binary execution ledger recording exact timestamps, operations attempted, preflight outcomes, verified bytes freed, errors encountered, and settled steps.
- **Native OS Handoffs**: Dispatches native Windows URI handlers and control panel applets: Storage Sense (`ms-settings:storagesense`), Installed Apps (`ms-settings:appsfeatures`), System Protection (`SystemPropertiesProtection.exe`), and Component Store guidance (DISM / Cleanmgr).

### 9. Headless CLI & Transport-Neutral Automation Interface
- **Command Family**:
  - `pigtree scan <target> [options]`: Execute scan and output snapshot or stream results.
  - `pigtree query <snapshot> [options]`: Execute typed queries against saved `.pts` files.
  - `pigtree verify <snapshot> [options]`: Run progressive duplicate content verification.
  - `pigtree plan create <snapshot> [options]`: Formulate an immutable Action Plan.
  - `pigtree plan validate <plan>`: Run Live Preflight re-observation on an Action Plan.
  - `pigtree execution run <plan> [options]`: Execute a validated Action Plan.
  - `pigtree execution recover <record>`: Inspect or execute recovery from an execution record.
- **Dual Stream Contracts**:
  - `stdout`: NDJSON for event streams, JSON for synchronous queries, and RFC 4180 CSV for tabular output.
  - `stderr`: Structured diagnostic messages, human-readable status logs, and error traces.
- **Normative CLI Exit Classes (ADR 0003)**:
  - `0`: `SUCCESS` - Operation finished with terminal success under selected policy and profile.
  - `1`: `OPERATION_FAILED` - Operation encountered fatal execution or platform error (earlier mutation steps may have committed).
  - `2`: `COMMAND_ERROR` - Malformed CLI arguments, invalid schema, or unsupported command.
  - `3`: `CANCELLED` - Operation cleanly cancelled by user or automation signal.
  - `4`: `COVERAGE_GAPS_PRESENT` - Operation finished, but policy-significant Coverage Gaps or incomplete observations are present.
  - `5`: `INTERACTION_REQUIRED` - Operation required user interaction, consent, or elevation not provided under non-interactive policy.
  - `6`: `PREFLIGHT_FAILED` - Action execution Live Preflight rejected one or more steps.

### 10. Privacy, Diagnostics, and Redaction Subsystem
- **Zero Remote Telemetry**: No network sockets, analytics libraries, or off-device telemetry services exist in any binary.
- **Diagnostic Generation**: Generates comprehensive local diagnostic packages containing OS version, filesystem types, driver details, engine crash dumps, and anonymized performance metrics.
- **Versioned Redaction Capabilities**:
  - `obfuscate_paths`: Replaces directory and file names with consistent pseudonyms while preserving directory hierarchy and tree depth.
  - `mask_user_identities`: Masks or strips Owner security principals and SID strings.
  - `scrub_native_messages`: Strips sensitive path arguments from native Win32/NT error strings.
- **Zero Mutation Authority**: Redacted outputs carry **zero execution authority for mutation**.

### 11. Packaging, Distribution, and Shell Integration
- **Runtime Deployment**: WPF client is compiled as a self-contained ReadyToRun (R2R) multi-file deployment targeting the latest supported .NET LTS on x64. Engine, CLI, and helper workers are compiled as optimized native Rust binaries.
- **Installer Modality**:
  - *Per-User MSI (Primary)*: Built with WiX v5, installs into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\PigTree` with zero UAC elevation prompts required.
  - *Per-Machine MSI (Enterprise)*: Optional standard elevated installer targeting `%ProgramFiles%\PigTree`.
  - *Portable ZIP*: Standalone, zero-dependency archive for USB drives and technician toolkits.
- **Shell Integration**:
  - Windows 11: Sparse Package with external location registering modern File Explorer context menu verbs ("Scan with PigTree").
  - Windows 10: Classic registry shell verbs (`HKCU\Software\Classes\Directory\shell\PigTree`).
  - File Associations: Registers `.pts` (Analysis Snapshot) and `.ptse` (Snapshot Enrichment) file types.

## Testing Decisions

### Testing Philosophy
Testing in PigTree emphasizes external behavioral verification across public boundaries rather than asserting private implementation details. Tests execute against stable interfaces and verify user-visible outcomes, domain invariants, error handling, and performance budgets.

### Primary Testing Seam: Transport-Neutral Shared Engine Contract
The primary and dominant behavioral testing seam across the entire product is the **Transport-Neutral Shared Engine Contract** (`pigtree-engine.exe`). Because the core domain logic, scanning orchestration, accounting reconciliation, query evaluation, duplicate detection, action plan formulation, live preflight verification, snapshot persistence, and mutation planning are encapsulated within the shared engine, the vast majority of functional test suites exercise this contract directly:
- **Scan & Ingestion Tests**: Validates that running scans across test directory fixtures correctly constructs Directory Entries, Filesystem Objects, Hard Link relationships, Content Streams, and Storage Characteristics.
- **Capacity Reconciliation Tests**: Asserts that whole-volume accounting rigorously balances Capacity, Free Space, Used Space, Accounted Unique Allocation, and Reconciliation Difference (Unattributed Used Space or Over-Accounted Allocation) across simulated disk environments.
- **Query Algebra Tests**: Evaluates typed filtering, size ranges, date boundaries, glob/regex matching, and three-valued logic against populated snapshot fixtures.
- **Duplicate Verification Tests**: Verifies multi-stage hashing, keeper selection algorithms, cloud hydration gates, and exact reclaimable allocation calculations.
- **Action Plan & Live Preflight Tests**: Tests action plan generation, invariant validation, preflight staleness detection (simulating file modifications, timestamp shifts, and file ID swaps), and execution recovery journals against mocked and temporary filesystem trees.
- **Snapshot Serialization Tests**: Validates zero-copy round-trip serialization and deserialization of `.pts` base snapshots and `.ptse` enrichment files, asserting CRC-32/BLAKE3 checksum verification and backward-compatibility rules.

### Prior Art & Prototype Harnesses
The test architecture directly builds upon the verification harnesses and domain test fixtures developed during the exploratory prototyping phase:
- **Core Analysis Workflow Prototype Fixtures**: Leverages the multi-scenario domain fixtures developed in the core analysis prototype (`prototypes/core-analysis-workflows`), validating hard-link aliasing accounting (e.g. WinSxS vs System32), online-only cloud placeholders, inaccessible System Volume Information coverage gaps, and summary remainder rows.
- **Duplicate Remediation Prototype Invariant Harness**: Leverages the 5-scenario stress tests developed in the duplicate remediation prototype (`prototypes/duplicate-remediation`), validating multi-stage verification pipelines, Mark-of-the-Web stream mismatches, hard-link alias deduplication exclusions, cloud hydration consent gates, and live preflight invalidation upon timestamp/size churn.

### Auxiliary Testing Seams
Where boundary behaviors cannot be proven at the primary shared engine contract, dedicated tests are established at narrow, well-defined auxiliary seams:
1. **Narrow Filesystem Adapter Seams**:
   - *Win32 Traversal Adapter*: Direct Win32 directory traversal tests covering deep directory nesting (> 260 characters / extended paths), junction loops, reparse tags, and access-denied handling.
   - *Raw MFT Parser Adapter*: Isolated parsing tests evaluating raw `$MFT` record chunks against synthetic and corrupted NTFS volume images, asserting strict fail-closed invariant validation and fallback signaling.
2. **Full IPC & Multi-Process Topology Seams**:
   - Integration tests executing real process spawns across all seven executables (`PigTree.exe`, `pigtree.exe`, `pigtree-engine.exe`, `pigtree-scan-worker.exe`, `pigtree-elevated-broker.exe`, `pigtree-raw-parser.exe`, `pigtree-mutation-worker.exe`).
   - Verifies Named Pipe lifecycle, Protocol Buffers framing, token SID validation, process crash recovery, and Job Object automatic termination.
3. **WPF UI Automation (UIA) & Accessibility Seams**:
   - End-to-end accessibility test suites utilizing Windows UI Automation testing frameworks (such as FlaUI or WinAppDriver).
   - Validates that the virtualized tree-grid and Direct3D 11 Treemap expose truthful, bounded UIA element trees, respond to keyboard focus/navigation, announce state changes to screen readers, handle `IVirtualizedItemProvider` realization and eviction cleanly, and function correctly under Windows High Contrast themes and 200% text scaling.
4. **Security Boundary & Privilege Seams**:
   - Tests asserting that standard workers execute with restricted security tokens and stripped write access.
   - Validates that the elevated scan broker acquires read-only handles without uncontracted parsing and closes immediately upon scan termination.
5. **Packaging, Distribution, and Shell Integration Seams**:
   - Automated installer test suites validating WiX v5 per-user and per-machine MSI installation, repair, upgrading, and clean uninstallation.
   - Asserts Sparse Package and registry shell context menu registration, `.pts` file association, and zero-dependency portable ZIP execution from read-only directories.
6. **Benchmark & Performance Regression Seams**:
   - Automated benchmark test suites executing standardized workloads on fixed test datasets (up to 5,000,000 entries).
   - Validates compliance with the performance targets defined in `docs/performance-targets.md`, measuring scan duration, memory usage, snapshot reopening latency, search query response times, and rendering framerates under controlled OS cache conditions (using RAMMap and cache flushing).
   - Comparative benchmark suite executing structured, side-by-side evaluations against named competitor baselines (WizTree and TreeSize).

## Out of Scope

The following capabilities are explicitly out of scope for PigTree v1.0 and are intentionally excluded from the release boundary:
1. **Non-Windows Platforms**: macOS, Linux, and mobile operating systems. PigTree v1.0 is engineered specifically for Windows 10 and 11 on x64 architectures.
2. **Remote Network Storage & Cloud Backends**: Direct scanning of remote SMB/NFS network shares, WebDAV, or cloud API endpoints (such as Microsoft Graph API, Google Drive API, Dropbox API) beyond local reparse point observation.
3. **Multi-Root Composite Scans**: Combining multiple independent root volumes or disjoint folders into one ambiguous accounting total (each Scan Target in v1.0 is strictly exactly one Volume or one Directory).
4. **Unmounted Virtual Disk Parsing**: Inspecting unmounted virtual-disk container images (`.vhd`, `.vhdx`, `.iso`, `.vmdk`) directly as filesystems without prior operating system mounting.
5. **Domain-Wide Enterprise Auditing & Attribution**: Domain-wide Active Directory owner/ACL compliance auditing, organization-wide storage quota enforcement, and enterprise multi-user attribution workflows beyond local volume security metadata.
6. **Rich Report Design & Scheduled Delivery Suites**: Complex visual report design and delivery suites (such as generating Excel workbooks with embedded macros, PDF/HTML dashboards, automated email delivery, custom reporting templates, and scheduled report UI wizards), whereas standard locale-neutral CSV and JSON/NDJSON data exports remain fully supported.
7. **Saved-Scan Comparisons, Growth Trends & VSS History**: Multi-snapshot differential comparison, storage growth trend analytics over time, and Volume Shadow Copy (VSS) snapshot historical analysis in v1.0, whereas saving and reopening individual standalone Historical Snapshots (`.pts`/`.ptse`) remains fully supported.
8. **Persistent Background Services & Real-Time Monitoring**: Daemon services, continuous background filesystem indexing, or real-time file change monitoring via persistent USN Journal watchers.
9. **Automated Scheduled Disk Cleaning**: Background task schedulers or unattended automated file deletion. All cleanup actions require interactive user review or explicit CLI script invocation.
10. **Arbitrary File Content Indexing & Search**: Full-text file content searching, indexing text inside documents, or semantic file search (PigTree indexes filesystem metadata and stream hashes, not internal file contents).
11. **Destructive System File Modification**: Forcing deletion or alteration of protected Windows OS components (such as `WinSxS`, `DriverStore`, `System Volume Information`). These are strictly routed to native Windows system tools.
12. **Automatic Remote Cloud Hydration**: Automatically downloading offline cloud files during analysis without explicit user consent.
13. **Commercial Licensing & Paywalls**: Proprietary editions, feature tiering, or commercial paywalls. PigTree is 100% open-source software.
14. **Off-Device Telemetry & User Tracking**: Cloud telemetry, user behavioral tracking, or remote analytics reporting.

## Further Notes

- **Provenance & Planning Context**: This specification directly synthesizes and formalizes the settled decisions and validated prototypes from GitHub issue #1 (*Define the PigTree product specification*) and its 14 completed child decision and research issues:
  - Inventory of competitor capabilities (issue #2)
  - Everyday workflows, pain points, and user journeys (issue #3)
  - Windows filesystem, scanning, and elevation facts (issue #4)
  - Windows UI technologies and accessibility evaluation (issue #5)
  - Benchmark evidence and reproducible measurement methodology (issue #6)
  - Product capability and release boundary definition (issue #7)
  - Canonical disk-space information model and accounting semantics (issue #8, `CONTEXT.md`)
  - Core analysis workflow prototype validation (issue #9)
  - Scanning subsystem and privilege architecture (issue #10, ADR 0001)
  - Shared engine and automation contract (issue #11, ADR 0003)
  - Guarded cleanup safety, action plans, and recovery (issue #12, ADR 0002)
  - Measurable product performance targets and acceptance budgets (issue #13, `docs/performance-targets.md`)
  - Production technology architecture selection (issue #14, ADR 0004)
  - Safe duplicate review and remediation prototype validation (issue #15)
- **Handoff to Implementation**: With all 14 planning milestones resolved and verified, this specification forms the authoritative foundation for downstream implementation planning, milestone scheduling, and issue breakdown.

`

items.title: ED-HMI2220-070C: black screen with stock driver bridge-init value 0x02; 0x01 restores display on affected unit
items.body: ### Describe the bug When installing and operating system, such as the latest Raspberry Pi OS release. The HMI will be blank. The HDMI port will work. The HMI will not. ### Steps to reproduce the behaviour reinstall an os, Or, after applying work around, unapply work around. same behavior. Issue may be present in certain specific versions ### Device (s) Ed-HMI2220-070c ### System pi@raspberrypi:~ $ cat /etc/os-release PRETTY_NAME="Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie)" NAME="Debian GNU/Linux" VERSION_ID="13" VERSION="13 (trixie)" VERSION_CODENAME=trixie DEBIAN_VERSION_FULL=13.7 ID=debian HOME_URL="https://www.debian.org/" SUPPORT_URL="https://www.debian.org/support" BUG_REPORT_URL="https://bugs.debian.org/" $ uname -a Linux raspberrypi 6.18.50+rpt-rpi-v8 #1 SMP PREEMPT Debian 1:6.18.50-1+rpt1 (2026-09-11) aarch64 GNU/Linux pi@raspberrypi:~ $ vcgencmd version Sep 14 2026 14:49:30 Copyright (c) 2012 Broadcom version a86983925695a7e63166327d7c002d64040ed31d (clean) (release) (start) pi@raspberrypi:~ $ cat /etc/rpi-issue Raspberry Pi reference 2026-10-06 Generated using pi-gen, https://github.com/RPi-Distro/pi-gen, b2cd98a9ee08a31ef7d0110ed09f2492bbd972ec, stage4 ### Logs _No response_ ### Additional context This issue may pertain to the 8GB or older models of the ED-HMI2220-070C From testing, the 32GB model is unaffected. **Environment:** - Hardware: EDATEC ED-HMI2220-070C, unit with 8 GB eMMC storage - OS: Debian GNU/Linux 13 (Trixie), using Raspberry Pi kernel packages - Kernel: 6.18.50+rpt-rpi-v8 - Driver: edatec_panel_regulator - Default overlay configuration ```config dtoverlay=vc4-kms-v3d [all] dtoverlay=vc4-kms-dsi-edatec-panel-070c,interrupt=7 ``` I followed [EDATEC application notes](https://edatec.cn/docs/an/an44-use-7-inch-and-10.1-inch-hmi-on-standard-rpi-os/), which describes support through the stock Raspberry Pi kernel and overlays. # Expected Behavior: The built-in display shows the console and desktop after boot. # Actual beahvior: The backlight turns on, but the screen remains black. HDMI output works. The kernel reports DSI-1 as connected and enabled at 1024×600. # workaround enable userspace i2c **sudo i2ctransfer -f -y 10 w2@0x27 0x11 0x01** Desktop appears instantly # suspected source Issue: https://github.com/raspberrypi/linux/blob/rpi-6.18.y/drivers/regulator/edatec-panel-regulator.c regmap_write(regmap, REG_BRIDGE_INIT, 0x02); is evidently incorrect for this unit model. # repeatability: **sudo i2ctransfer -f -y 10 w2@0x27 0x11 0x02** setting the value back to its initial setting will reproduce the issue, if the HMI is fully powered off, then restarted. simply running the command will not produce the initial behavior. # Proposal for resolution: Please investigate whether the bridge-initialization value needs to be selected according to the panel-controller revision or exposed through a device-tree property, rather than fixed at 0x02 for all supported units. ## I only have 8GB and 32GB models of this device, and I am not saying there is some correlation between disk space and video driver issues. This issue may effect various unit models, older or newer models, I'm not really sure. The ones with the blue label, maybe that indicates something relevant to the appropriate person. I have not compiled a specific hardware variants list that might compare hardware differences, or versions of this device, and the device itself is not clearly labeled. All I can verify is that I have some 8GB models of The Ed-HMI2220-070c device, and they are effected by this condition. # Reference Material: https://edatec.cn/docs/an/an44-use-7-inch-and-10.1-inch-hmi-on-standard-rpi-os/#_2-2-configuration-instructions

items.title: [Package]: OpenPGP-compatible/FreePG-patched GnuPG
items.body:
### Why is it worth to add this package?

The target userbase of termux are people seeking to utilize a linux-like terminal on their android phone. Hence there are likely a multitude of users relying on PGP.
From December 2022 and onwards, the original GnuPG diverges from the newest OpenPGP standard. This can cause long term compatibility issues.
The [arch wiki ](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/GnuPG#OpenPGP_compatibility) has a good explanation of the background of these issues. [OpenPGP.com](https://www.openpgp.org/about/gnupg/) also explains the issue.
Having a package that includes FreePG-patched GnuPG ensures that users can utilize their needed version of GnuPG without compatibility issues.
Several distributions, [including Arch, Debian, Fedora, NixOS, Ubuntu and Gentoo already offer packages with FreePG patched- GnuPG.](https://freepg.org/) and have done so for many years.


### Home page URL

https://freepg.org/

### Source code URL

https://gitlab.com/freepg/gnupg

### Packaging policy acknowledgement

- [x] The project is actively developed.
- [x] The project has [existing packages](https://repology.org/projects/) and is "well known".
- [x] Licensed under an [open source license](https://spdx.org/licenses/).
- [x] Not available through a language package manager: cargo, cpan, dotnet tool, gem, npm, pip, etc.

- [x] Not taking up too much disk space (< 100MiB per architecture, exceptions can be made)
- [x] Not duplicating the functionality of existing packages.
- [x] Not serving hacking, malware, phishing, spamming, spying, ddos functionality.
- [x] I certify that I have read [Termux Packaging Policy](https://github.com/termux/termux-packages/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#packaging-policy) and understand that my request will be denied if it is found lacking.

### Additional information

I understand the Arch Linux build system, but am not thoroughly well versed in the build process of termux. I nonetheless attempted to look through [the official package for GnuPG](https://github.com/termux/termux-packages/tree/master/packages/gnupg) to double-check if FreePG patches were already implemented, and it seemed they were not.
